answer: Dear Client,The overlapping in service in respect of previous and present establishment and any anomaly or discrepancy in EPF records of any registered member may be a ground for future dispute. When your EPF record shows an anomaly in the joining and exit date in both the previous and present Company which is contradictory, then until and unless those anomalies are rectified by the concerned employers, PF records will show overlapping or dual employment. A joint declaration form is used to correct Provident Fund (PF) member details. It is a combined form that the employee and employer sign and submit to the regional PF commissioner to update the wrong information entered in the employeesâ PF accounts. An employee cannot update the service history. Only an employer can rectify the error in the employment record of the EPFO. So if an employee finds an error in the database, he should contact their present or previous employers and get it corrected. In the given situation, to resolve the issue of overlapping in the P F records of both employers, you need to approach the office of the Regional P F Commissioner who is the competent authority to resolve any anomaly arising out of the date of appointment and date of discharge in EPF records. An individual can file a complaint using the EPF i-Grievance Management System (www. https://epfigms.gov.in/). Once you succeed in wiping out the stigma of dual employment from your EPF records with the cooperation of your previous and present employer, your scope of employment with other companies will be restored with clean employment records. If the complaint is not resolved even on receipt of JDF, you can approach the Employeesâ Provident Funds Appellate Tribunal (EPFAT) which was constituted under the provisions of the Section 7 D of the EPF and M P Act 1952, Now, as per the Finance Act 2017, the Employees' Provident Fund Appellate Tribunal has been merged with Central Government Industrial Tribunal w.e.f. 26.05.2017. So, if no relief yields from the office of the PF Commissioner, you may approach the Central Government Industrial Tribunal for appropriate relief. In case of non-cooperation from both previous and current employers which amounted to unfair labour practice, you may bring the matter to the notice of the the concerned Labour Commissioner or Asst. Labour Commissioner/LEO/Chief Inspector(Shops and Establishment) for a resolution in the matter.

answer: Dear Client,A service/employment bond itself does not create any relationship between an employer and an employee unless and until it is followed by the essential steps required to make the Bond valid and enforceable under the law. The validity of Employment bonds can be challenged based on Section 27 of the Indian Contract Act,1872 which prohibits any agreement in restraint of trade and profession. The law states that an agreement (employment bond) will be illegal only if it restrains someone from exercising a lawful profession/ trade/ business. As per the mandate of Section 27 of the Indian Contract Act,1872, any terms and conditions of an agreement that directly or indirectly compels the employee to serve the employer or puts a restriction on them joining the competitor or other employer is not valid. The employee has the right to resign from the employment even if he has agreed to the employment bond to serve the employer for a specific period. In the case where the employer can prove that the employee is joining the competitor to disclose the trade secret then the court may issue an injunction order restricting the employee from joining the competitor. Further, Section 73 of the Act makes provision for un-liquidated damages (not stipulated in a contract), Section 74 deals with liquidated damages (stipulated in a contract), and no compensation is attracted for mere breach of contract u/s.73. 74 of the Act unless such breach resulted in an actual loss or damage to the opposite party employer. So, in the prevailing situation, if you are not holding a position of manager or supervisor in the Company, but a workman as defined under Sec.2(s) of the Industrial Dispute Act, 1947. serving a legal notice to the Company reach out to the office of the concerned Labour Commissioner or the office of the Chief Inspector, Shops and Establishments, as the case may be, to file a complaint against the company over alleged unfair labour practice for redressal of your grievance, Further, SAMADHAN Portal was launched by the Ministry of Labour and Employment for facilitating filing of industrial disputes by the workmen, employers and trade unions under the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947. The online portal has a user-friendly interface and has enhanced transparency and efficiency of grievance resolution for all stakeholders. The workmen/trade unions/management can file their disputes and claims by logging into the portal through the UMANG app and also by visiting the nearest Common Services Centres. But, if you are holding the position of Manager or Administrator in the Company, you have to file a civil suit against the Company before the Civil Court seeking appropriate relief in the matter.

answer: Dear Client,From the prolonged contents of the query, it is unclear what type of legal remedies for a cause of action you sought from a counsel. However, be informed that a complaint can be filed with Lokpal of India in terms of provisions under 2(e) of the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013, for the offenses alleged to have been committed by a public servant under the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988 such as offences relating to public servant being bribed, taking undue advantage to influence public servant by corrupt or illegal means or by the exercise of personal influence, Offence relating to bribing of a public servant, Public servant obtaining (undue advantage), without consideration from person concerned in proceeding or business transacted by such public servant, Criminal misconduct by a public servant. In terms of provisions under Section 53, of the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013, a complaint should be made within seven years from the date on which the offense mentioned in the complaint is alleged to have been committed. A complaint is required to be filed in the prescribed form annexed with the Lokpal (Complaint) Rules, 2020. The complaint can be filed online through the Lokpal Online portal. A fillable complaint form is also available at (https://lokpal.gov.in/pdfs/complaint_form.docx). Under Section 19 of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988, sanction for prosecution is required for an offence punishable under Sections 7, 10, 11, 13, 15 of the Act, while under Section 197(1) Cr. P.C. sanction is required for an offence committed by a public servant while acting or purporting to act in the discharge of his official duty, and not otherwise. After the amendment of the Prevention of Corruption Act, in 2018, it significantly extended the provisions of PCA and gave it the required edge to tackle bribery/corruption involving commercial entities/private companies. According to Section 9 of the amended Act, a commercial organization can be held liable âif any person associated with such commercial organization gives or promises to give any undue advantage to a public servantâ with an intent to obtain or retain business or any advantage for that commercial organization. This provision covers all types of entities (including domestic companies, foreign companies, and partnerships) doing business in India. Thus, while the PCA, 1988 applied to public sector employees, the Act has been amended to encompass situations where private organizations and individuals can also be held accountable for indulging in corrupt practices. Further, the CBI investigates cases of corruption in compliance with the provisions of the Prevention of Corruption Act 1988, under the supervision of the Central Vigilance Commission (CVC). This can include cases of bribery, extortion, and other forms of corruption. The CBI has a special division called the Anti-Corruption Branch (ACB). This branch handles the investigation of corruption-related cases. The CBI can initiate suo moto investigations on the basis of information received from the public, the media, or other sources. CBI lays great emphasis on catching corrupt public servants who demand and take bribes. The process of catching such corrupt public servants red-handed while they demand and take bribes is popularly called the 'trap'. It is not a legal term. A set procedure has been devised in CBI to lay a trap against a corrupt public servant. The evidence collected during the process of trap is placed before the court along with the charge sheet and is quite important in securing the conviction of the public servant charged with corruption. So, given the proposition of relevant laws, you may choose the recourse/steps that suit your grievance most in the prevailing situation, If required, hire an experienced Advocate to navigate the issues in the right way.

question: if I don't give money to my contract company after working 5 months they terminating me giving wrong excuse( South West Delhi, Delhi )
answer: Dear Client,Giving or taking a bribe for any purpose is a criminal offence, but it cannot be grounds for termination from employment unless it is proven. Termination or dismissal other than a disciplinary action for proven misconduct amounts to illegal termination/ retrenchment and is defined as an industrial dispute under Section 2A of the Industrial Dispute Act, 1947 which also violated the mandatory provision of Sec.25F and 25N of the I D Act that prescribed certain conditions to comply with by the employer before termination/retrenchment of a workman/employee from the employment. Under Chapters V-A & V-B of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947, for retrenchment of a workman of an industrial establishment employing below 100 workmen, an employer has to serve one month's notice or wages in lieu of notice. Even as per Clause 13(1) of the model Standing Order under Industrial Employment(Standing Orders) Act, 1946, for terminating the employment of a permanent workman, notice in writing shall be given either by the employer or the workman one month's notice in the case of monthly rated workmen and two weeks' notice in the case of other workmen; one month's or two week's pay, as the case may be, may be paid in lieu of notice. In that scenario, serving a legal notice to the employer, the terminated employee/workman can raise an industrial dispute before the concerned Labour Commissioner for redressal of the complaint failing which he can approach directly the Industrial Tribunal/Labor Court concerned for adjudication seeking reinstatement with back wages and other service-linked benefits provided he is not holding the position of Manager/Supervisor but a workman as defined u/s.2(s) of the Industrial Dispute Act. Otherwise, in case he is holding the position of Manager/Administrative Officer in the Company, he has to file a civil suit before the Civil Court seeking appropriate relief in the matter.

After he got transferred to treasury department he was offered his salary that was same as his previous post in employment department. Recently a few days back he was issued a GO stating that he was not eligible for FR22 (a) (iv) and that his pay scale was to be rearranged. This will result in my dad's salary reduction by Rs.30,000. 
Is this a valid consequence. If not, how can we address this?( Mahbubnagar, Telangana )
answer: Dear Client,As per Office Memo No.DOPT-1669266628362 dated 24 November 2022, issued by the Department of Personnel and Training, Government of India, and the Ministry of Finance OM No. 3379-E.III (B)/65 dated the 17th June, 1965, read with proviso to FR 22-B, in cases of appointment of a Government servant to another post in Government on acceptance of technical resignation in the existing post acquiring a lien on a post will cease to hold any lien previously acquired on any other post. A permanent Government servant appointed in another Central Government Department/Office/ State Government has to resign from his parent department unless he reverts to that department within a period of 2 years, or 3 years. An undertaking to abide by this condition may be taken from him at the time of forwarding his application to other departments/offices. The benefit of past service is allowed in such cases subject to the fulfillment of the following conditions: (i) the Government servant should intimate the details of such application immediately on their joining; (ii) the Government servant at the time of resignation should specifically make a request, indicating that he is resigning to take up another appointment under the Government for which he applied before joining the Government service; (iii) the authority accepting the resignation should satisfy itself that had the employee been in service on the date of application for the post mentioned by the employee, his application would have been forwarded through proper channel. In your father's case if these qualifying criteria are met and despite his entitlement, if the reduction of wages is caused, then your father can make a grievance before the HOD and if that grievance yields no result, your father can approach the concerned bench of the Central Administrative Tribunal(CAT) by filing an application in Form - I under sub-rule 1 Rule 4 of the Central Administrative Tribunal (Procedure) Rules, 1987 seeking appropriate relief in the matter. However, before approaching the CAT, the merit of the claim may please be reviewed by an Advocate experienced in CAT/SAT matters.

question: Sir, I am a army person and will retire after 2 years and I have 3 child, so can i will  be eligible for central govt job after retirement.( Jaipur, Rajasthan )
answer: Dear Client,The Ex-Seerviceman (Re-employment in Central Civil Services and Posts) Rules, 1979 as modified by the Gazette Notification dated 2P Oct. 1986., defines an ex-serviceman as a person who has served in any rank whether as combatant or non-combatant in the Regular Army, Navy and Air force of the Indian Union. Ten percent of the vacancies in the posts of the level of Assistant Commandant in all para-military forces, ten percent of the vacancies in each of the categories of Group 'C' and of such posts in each Group 'C' service; and twenty percent of the vacancies in each of the categories of Group 'D' posts and of such posts in each Group 'D' service, including permanent vacancies filled initially temporarily and temporary vacancies which are likely to be made permanent or are likely to continue for three months and more, to be filled by direct recruitment in any year shall be reserved for being filled by ex-servicemen. There is no specific mention of 3 children of an ex-serviceman barring him from availing the reservation of central Govt jobs post-retirement. However, in a recent judgment, the Supreme Court upheld the decision of the Rajasthan Government to disqualify a candidate from applying to a police constable post for having more than two children. The Court held that Rule 24(4) of the Rajasthan Police Subordinate Service Rules, 1989, which provides that âno candidate shall be eligible for appointment to the service who has more than two children on or after 01.06.2002. Rule Disqualifying Candidate Having More Than 2 Children From Govt Job Doesn't Violate Constitution of India. So, considering the rulings of the Supreme Court, you should clarify the matter from the Department of Personnel and Training(DOPT), MINISTRY OF PERSONNEL, PUBLIC GRIEVANCES AND PENSIONS, Government of India.

question: I have did dual employment without knowing it will effect my career my PF is getting overlap now and no one is hiring. Have approached regional commissioner seeking help but no one is helping to resolve this issue please help( Hyderabad, Telangana )
answer: Dear Client,Before joining another Company you are required to tender your resignation and to obtain a relieving letter from the earlier company serving the notice period as per the terms of employment that eventually caused the overlapping of service. The overlapping in service in respect of previous and present establishment and any anomaly or discrepancy in EPF records of any registered member may be a ground for future dispute. When your EPF record shows an anomaly in the joining and exit date in both the previous and present Company which is contradictory, then until and unless those anomalies are rectified by the concerned employers, PF records will show overlapping or dual employment. A joint declaration form is used to correct Provident Fund (PF) member details. It is a combined form that the employee and employer sign and submit to the regional PF commissioner to update the wrong information entered in the employeesâ PF accounts. An employee cannot update the service history. Only an employer can rectify the error in the employment record of the EPFO. So if an employee finds an error in the database, he should contact their present or previous employers and get it corrected. In the given situation, to resolve the issue of overlapping in the P F records of both employers, you need to approach the office of the Regional P F Commissioner who is the competent authority to resolve any anomaly arising out of the date of appointment and date of discharge in EPF records. An individual can file a complaint using the EPF i-Grievance Management System (www. https://epfigms.gov.in/). Once you succeed in wiping out the stigma of dual employment from your EPF records with the cooperation of your previous and present employer, your scope of employment with other companies will be restored with clean employment records. If the complaint is not resolved even on receipt of JDF, you can approach the Employeesâ Provident Funds Appellate Tribunal (EPFAT) which was constituted under the provisions of the Section 7 D of the EPF and M P Act 1952, Now, as per the Finance Act 2017, the Employees' Provident Fund Appellate Tribunal has been merged with Central Government Industrial Tribunal w.e.f. 26.05.2017. So, if no relief yields from the office of the PF Commissioner, you may approach the Central Government Industrial Tribunal for appropriate relief. In case of non-cooperation from both previous and current employers which amounted to unfair labour practice, you may bring the matter to the notice of the the concerned Labour Commissioner or Asst. Labour Commissioner/LEO/Chief Inspector(Shops and Establishment) for a resolution in the matter.

question:
My employment was recently terminated by my former employer, and as per the terms of my offer letter, they are obligated to provide notice period salary in case of termination. However, I have not received any such payment to date.  
 I am considering requesting compensation in addition to the notice period salary. I have not yet sent any communication to the employer requesting clarification or payment.
Could you advise on the best course of action to address this issue, including issuing a legal notice if necessary? I want to ensure that I proceed in a way that upholds my rights effectively.( Pune, Maharashtra )
answer: Dear Client,Termination or dismissal other than a disciplinary action for proven misconduct amounts to illegal termination/ retrenchment and is defined as an industrial dispute under Section 2A of the Industrial Dispute Act, 1947 which also violated the mandatory provision of Sec.25F and 25N of the I D Act that prescribed certain conditions to comply with by the employer before termination/retrenchment of a workman/employee from the employment. Under Chapters V-A & V-B of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947, for retrenchment of a workman of an industrial establishment employing below 100 workmen, an employer has to serve one month's notice or wages in lieu of notice. Even as per Clause 13(1) of the model Standing Order under Industrial Employment(Standing Orders) Act, 1946, for terminating the employment of a permanent workman, notice in writing shall be given either by the employer or the workman one month's notice in the case of monthly rated workmen and two weeks' notice in the case of other workmen; one month's or two week's pay, as the case may be, may be paid in lieu of notice. In that scenario, serving a legal notice to the employer, the terminated employee/workman can raise an industrial dispute before the concerned Labour Commissioner for redressal of the complaint failing which he can approach directly the Industrial Tribunal/Labor Court concerned for adjudication seeking reinstatement with back wages and other service-linked benefits provided he is not holding the position of Manager/Supervisor but a workman as defined u/s.2(s) of the Industrial Dispute Act. Otherwise, in case he is holding the position of Manager/Administrative Officer in the Company, he has to file a civil suit before the Civil Court seeking appropriate relief in the matter.

question: I decided to quit TCS after 5 days, but I don't want to pay the bond amount, but the HR told me that he will only accept the resignation mail if I mention paying the bond amount. What should i do?( Noida, Uttar Pradesh )
answer: Dear Client,Please go through the terms and conditions of your appointment letter and the service bond executed by you that governs your relationship with the company. A service/employment bond itself does not create any relationship between an employer and an employee unless and until it is followed by the essential steps required to make the Bond valid and enforceable under the law. The validity of service bonds can be challenged by invoking Section 27 of the Indian Contract Act,1872 which prohibits any agreement in restraint of trade and profession. The law states that an agreement (service/employment bond) will be illegal only if it restrains someone from exercising a lawful profession/ trade/ business. As per the mandate of Section 27 of the Indian Contract Act,1872, any terms and conditions of an agreement that directly or indirectly compels the employee to serve the employer or puts a restriction on them joining the competitor or other employer is not valid. The employee has the right to resign from the employment even if he has agreed to the service/employment bond to serve the employer for a specific period. In the case where the employer can prove that the employee is joining the competitor to disclose the trade secret then the court may issue an injunction order restricting the employee from joining the competitor. Further, Section 73 of the Act makes provision for un-liquidated damages (not stipulated in a contract), Section 74 deals with liquidated damages (stipulated in a contract), and no compensation is attracted for mere breach of contract u/s.73. 74 of the Act unless such breach resulted in an actual loss or damage to the opposite party employer. So, in the prevailing situation, if you are not holding a position of manager or supervisor in the Company, but a workman as defined under Sec.2(s) of the Industrial Dispute Act, 1947. serving a legal notice to the Company reach out to the office of the concerned Labour Commissioner or the office of the Chief Inspector, Shops and Establishments, as the case may be, to file a complaint against the company over alleged unfair labour practice for redressal of your grievance, But, if you are holding the position of Manager or Administrator in the Company, you have to file a civil suit against the Company before the Civil Court seeking desired relief in the matter. If required, reach out to an Advocate experienced in service matters for guidance and steps. Be informed that to restrict IT Companies from exploiting their employees by playing double standards, the Division Bench of the Karnataka High Court in the case of Commissioner of Income Tax v. Texas Instruments India Pvt Ltd (2021) 435 ITR unambiguously held that the IT sector employees considered to be "workmen" under Section 2(s) of the Industrial Dispute Act, 1947. Further, the Hon'ble Bombay High Court in the case of Godrej and Boyce Manufacturing Company Ltd. v. Shivkranti Kamgar Sanghatana, 2024 SCC OnLine Bom 938, decided on 28-03-2024 ruled out that the nature of duties and functions is the determining factor in ascertaining âworkmanâ under S. 2(s) of Industrial Disputes Act, 1947.

question: I have been terminated from a public listed company within 1 month of joining and that too without any prior notice or any reason of termination. How I can compensation till my retirement from the company, as I joined company at the age of 56 and retirement age is 60 year. I was appointed in a senior management  position.( Jaipur, Rajasthan )
answer: Dear Client,A termination may be considered illegal and unjustified if it breaches the terms of the contract or appointment letter by either party to the said contract. You joined a company(PSU) at the age of 56 years and were terminated after a month without serving any show-cause notice or holding any inquiry into misconduct, if any. Termination or dismissal other than a disciplinary action for proven misconduct amounts to illegal termination/ retrenchment and is defined as an industrial dispute under Section 2A of the Industrial Dispute Act, 1947 which also violated the mandatory provision of Sec.25F and 25N of the I D Act that prescribed certain conditions to comply with by the employer before termination/retrenchment of a workman/employee from the employment. Any Termination of a workman is covered under the Industrial Disputes Act and it falls under âRetrenchmentâ. In the case of Punjab Land Development Corporation Vs Labour Court, 1990 (II) LLJ, 70 SC, the Supreme Court held that The expression âretrenchmentâ is not to be understood in its narrow, natural and contextual meaning, but is to be understood in its wider, literal meaning to mean termination of service of a workman for any reason whatsoever. Further, in the case of Santosh Gupta Vs State Bank of Patiala AIR 1980 SC 1219, the Supreme Court ruled that the expression retrenchment must include every termination of the services of a workman by an act of the employer. In that scenario, serving a legal notice to the Employer/company, the terminated employee being a PSU employee, can approach the concerned bench of the Central Administrative Tribunal(CAT) by filing an application in Form - I under sub-rule 1 of Rule 4 of the Central Administrative Tribunal (Procedure) Rules, 1987 seeking appropriate order in the matter and if the CAT passes any adverse order, you can challenge the order through an appeal before the High Court seeking appropriate relief based on the merit of the dispute. Reach out to an Advocate experienced in CAT matters for necessary advice and steps.

question:
My father worked as a permanent employee in the Indian Railways. He joined in 2002 and retired in 2012. Before becoming a permanent employee, he worked in a contractor role. As per a Supreme Court ruling regarding contractor-to-permanent employee transitions, he officially should have been recognized as joining in 2000. Looking forward to your response.( Asansol, West Bengal )
answer: Dear Client,The Hon'ble Supreme Court has ruled that casual workers are also entitled to social security benefits as there should be no discrimination between contractual and permanent employees by their employer. The services of Contractual Employee can be counted towards qualifying service for Grant of Pension, Post Regularization as per Himachal Pradesh High Courtâs recent decision in Sheela Devi versus. State of HP & Ors. In CWPOA  No. 195/2019 by J Tarlok Singh Chauhan & J Chander Bhushan Barowalia.  As per Notification No. 26 (3)-Pension Unit/82, dated the 26th August, 1983 issued by Deptt. of Personnel & A.R, Govt. of India and published in the Gazette of India, dated the 10th September, 1983, as S.O. No. 3478, and as per Rue 5(3) of the Payment of Arrears of Pension (Nomination) Rules, 1983. every employee who is due to retire after the date of commencement of these rules shall submit the nomination, in triplicate, in Form "A" to the Head of Office or the Department from where he is retiring within three months before or after the date of retirement. According to sub-rule 7 of Rule 5, Nomination, fresh nomination or notice of modification of nomination shall take effect from the date of receipt thereof by the Pension Disbursing Authority or the Head of Office, as the case may be. Further, as per Rule 6, a nomination made under Rule 5 and accepted by the Pension Disbursing Authority or the Head of Office, shall be conclusive proof with regard to the person nominated to receive arrears of pension of the pensioner under these rules and the Office Memos are applicable to a pensioner under the new pension scheme subject to submission of Form I under Rule 10 within 6 months of resuming the govt. service or after retirement from the service. So, given the relevant notification and rules, first, be ensured whether your father complied with the provision of nomination in favour of your mother before or after his retirement from the service of railways or after the conversion of status of employment from contractual to permanent. In case such statutory formalities are complied with, you may escalate your grievance before the Secretary to the Ministry of Home Affairs (Department of Personnel and Administrative Reforms) and the Ministry of Personnel Pension & Public Grievance Department of Pension & Pensionersâ Welfare either online or offline mode. In case no favorable or satisfactory response is received from the concerned Deptts, then you can consider filing an application before the Central Administrative Tribunal(CAT) for redressal of the grievance following the provision of the Administrative Tribunals Act, 1985 and the Central Administrative Tribunal (Procedure) Rules, 1987. Rule 4 of the Central Administrative Tribunal (Procedure) Rules, 1987 prescribes the procedure for applying before the Registrar of the concerned bench of the CAT.  So, try to get the matter reviewed by an expert professional before approaching the CAT.

question: I have worked in a manufacturing company for 9 years and as per Payslip my joining date is 1.05.2016 when my EPF account was started.I gave an immediate resignation email 4 months ago but they refused to give any acceptance and did not reply back to my mail . Can they refused to give gratuity as I resigned without service notice period and also I didn't have any contract or appointment letter mentioned to serve a notice period.( Kolkata, West Bengal )
answer: Dear Client,The question of serving a notice period does not arise in the absence of any specific stipulation in the appointment letter requiring an employee to serve a notice period upon submission of resignation. According to Section 4(1) of the Payment of Gratuity Act of 1972, gratuity must be paid to an employee upon cessation of employment if he or she has rendered continuous service for five years or more. When you are in continuous service for more than 9 years before the resignation, you are eligible for payment of gratuity from the initial date of employment, i.e., 01/05/2016 to the date of your resignation. Section 4(2) of the Act provides that for every completed year of service or part thereof in excess of 6 months, the employer shall pay gratuity to an employee at the prescribed rates. Under Rule 7(1) of the Payment of Gratuity Rules, 1972, an employee who is eligible for payment of gratuity under the Act, or any person authorized, in writing, to act on his behalf, shall apply, within thirty days from the date the gratuity became payable, in Form 'I' to the employer who is duty bound to disburse the gratuity within 30 days of cessation of employment of employee or claim made by an employee. After the completion of 30 days, the employer has to pay you not only the gratuity amount but also the simple interest accrued for the delay in payment of the gratuity. In case of denial of gratuity by the employer, serving a legal notice to the company, reach out to the office of the concerned Labour Commissioner and the Controlling Authority under the Act to file a complaint against the employer over non-payment of gratuity despite your eligibility to redress the grievance. Under Sub-Sec.5 of Section 7 of the Act, the Controlling Authority is empowered with the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 to try the claim of the applicant and pass an order/direction on the claim petition. If required, you may hire an Advocate experienced in service matters to navigate the issue in the right way.

question:
I am a central govt employee since 2 years. I have applied for state govt service and intimated the department for NOC. But they refused and I have mentioned in application form my current employer.
So in the document process they are asking me for NOC certificate 
So what I do now?( Dausa, Rajasthan )
answer: Dear Client,As per Office Memo No.DOPT-1669266628362 dated 24 November 2022, issued by the Department of Personnel and Training, Government of India, and the Ministry of Finance OM No. 3379-E.III (B)/65 dated the 17th June, 1965, read with proviso to FR 22-B, in cases of appointment of a Government servant to another post in Government on acceptance of technical resignation in the existing post. Be informed that the resignation is treated as a technical formality where a Government servant has applied through a proper channel with an NOC for a post in the same or some other Department and is on selection, required to resign from the previous post for administrative reasons. The resignation will be treated as technical resignation if these conditions are met. Resignation in other cases including where competent authority has not allowed the Government servant to forward the application through proper channels will not be treated as a technical resignation. As per DOPT's OM dated 24/11/2022, a Government servant acquiring a lien on a post will cease to hold any lien previously acquired on any other post. A permanent Government servant appointed in another Central Government Department/Office/ State Government has to resign from his parent department unless he reverts to that department within a period of 2 years, or 3 years. An undertaking to abide by this condition may be taken from him at the time of forwarding his application to other departments/offices. Being the position as stated above you may seek further clarification on the subject from the concerned Deptt (DOPT). Hence it is advisable before moving ahead with litigation, you need to represent the grievance before the Head of the Deptt. for a resolution failing which, you can approach the concerned bench Central Administrative Tribunal(CAT) seeking appropriate relief in the matter. Rule 4 of the Central Administrative Tribunal (Procedure) Rules, 1987 prescribes the procedure for applying before the Registrar of the concerned bench of the CAT. This forum has been established to adjudicate disputes concerning recruitment and conditions of service for persons appointed for public services. So, try to get the matter reviewed by an expert professional before challenging the action of the establishment before approaching the CAT.

answer: Dear Client,As per the Ministry of Finance Office Memo No. 3379-E.III (B)/65 dated the 17th June 1965, the resignation is treated as a technical resignation where a Government servant has applied through proper channels for a post in the same or some other Department and is on selection, required to resign the previous post for administrative reasons. The resignation will be treated as technical resignation if these conditions are met. Resignation in other cases including where competent authority has not allowed the Government servant to forward the application through proper channels will not be treated as a technical resignation and the benefit of past service will not be admissible. The benefit of past service is allowed in such cases subject to the fulfillment of the following conditions: (i) the Government servant should intimate the details of such application immediately on their joining; (ii) the Government servant at the time of resignation should specifically make a request, indicating that he is resigning to take up another appointment under the Government for which he applied before joining the Government service; (iii) the authority accepting the resignation should satisfy itself that had the employee been in service on the date of application for the post mentioned by the employee, his application would have been forwarded through proper channel. As per DOPT's OM dated 24/11/2022, a Government servant acquiring a lien on a post will cease to hold any lien previously acquired on any other post. A permanent Government servant appointed in another Central Government Department/Office/ State Government has to resign from his parent department unless he reverts to that department within a period of 2 years, or 3 years. An undertaking to abide by this condition may be taken from him at the time of forwarding his application to other departments/offices. Being the position as stated above, when your technical resignation was rejected by the Railway, you lost your lien on the post of your previous employment by the effluxion of time and there are no other remedies feasible to regain the loss of lien on your previous of employment under railway.

I have also reached my previous employer, but they don't have any options to modify the date, can you please suggest how to correct this date overlap, I have all the documents from my previous company.

I was struggling for past 4 months due to this problem, even if I ask PF office they told, this employer is not under their jurisdiction, so we can't help on this. Please kindly share any suggestions, that would be really helpful.( Chennai, Tamil Nadu )
answer: Dear Client,The overlapping in service in respect of previous and present establishment and any anomaly or discrepancy in EPF records of any registered member may be a ground for future dispute. When your EPF record shows an anomaly in the joining and exit date in both the previous and present Company which is contradictory, then until and unless those anomalies are rectified by the concerned employers, PF records will show overlapping. In the given scenario, to resolve the issue of overlapping in the P F records, you can approach the office of the Regional P F Commissioner under whose jurisdiction both of your previous and present employers belong. The RPFC is the competent authority to resolve any anomaly/discrepancy arising out of the date of appointment and date of exit of an employee in EPF records. An individual member of EPF can file a complaint using the EPF i-Grievance Management System (www. https://epfigms.gov.in/). or filing a complaint offline in the office of the Regional PF Commissioner concerned. If the complaint is not resolved before the authority, you can approach the Employeesâ Provident Funds Appellate Tribunal (EPFAT) which was constituted under the provisions of the Section 7 D of the EPF and M P Act 1952, Now, as per the Finance Act 2017, the Employees' Provident Fund Appellate Tribunal has been merged with Central Government Industrial Tribunal w.e.f. 26.05.2017. So, if no relief yields from the office of the Regl. PF Commissioner, you may approach the Central Government Industrial Tribunal for appropriate relief.

question: In december 2022, i have joined as PA stenographer in district court and i have technically resigned to join state public service as PA stenographer in august 2024. As i have no lien can i revert back my parent department if they wish to take back me again.( Agartala, Tripura )
answer: Dear Client,As per the Ministry of Finance Office Memo No. 3379-E.III (B)/65 dated the 17th June, 1965, the resignation is treated as a technical resignation where a Government servant has applied through proper channels for a post in the same or some other Department and is on selection, required to resign the previous post for administrative reasons. The resignation will be treated as technical resignation if these conditions are met. The benefit of past service, if otherwise admissible under rules, may be given in such cases. Resignation in other cases including where competent authority has not allowed the Government servant to forward the application through proper channels will not be treated as a technical resignation and the benefit of past service will not be admissible. The benefit of past service is allowed in such cases subject to the fulfillment of the following conditions: (i) the Government servant should intimate the details of such application immediately on their joining; (ii) the Government servant at the time of resignation should specifically make a request, indicating that he is resigning to take up another appointment under the Government for which he applied before joining the Government service; (iii) the authority accepting the resignation should satisfy itself that had the employee been in service on the date of application for the post mentioned by the employee, his application would have been forwarded through proper channel. As per DOPT's OM dated 24/11/2022, a Government servant acquiring a lien on a post will cease to hold any lien previously acquired on any other post. A permanent Government servant appointed in another Central Government Department/Office/ State Government has to resign from his parent department unless he reverts to that department within a period of 2 years, or 3 years. An undertaking to abide by this condition may be taken from him at the time of forwarding his application to other departments/offices. Being the position as stated above you may seek further clarification on the subject from the concerned Deptt (DOPT) or apply to the parent department for consideration.

question: Hi, My ex employer has made mistakes while submitting the PF amount. Though the EPS applicability was Yes for me, but while submitting the PF amount, my employer has mistakenly not deposited anything in to the pension head for three years. Now they have submitted the revised document with the local PF office. Its been months. But every time i check the status of the same with the PF office by raising grievance in the EPF system, it is still not done. I am looking to withdraw my PF. But i am not able to do the same due to this mistake, I don't know what to to do expedite the same and withdraw my PF.( Bhubaneswar, Orissa )
answer: Dear sir,PF  PROVIDENT FUNDHow to solve the two UAN problem?Note that each person should have only one UAN number (like PAN), hence if you have multiple UAN, itâs not allowed and creates problem in the EPF system, because is no proper track. Hence, as soon as you come to know that there are multiple UAN assigned to you, you should cancel one of the UAN (mostly the old UAN) or should try to deactivate one of themProcess to deactivate old UANStep #1 â The first step if that you should start the EPF transfer for all the EPFâs which are not under the latest UAN generated. This can be done using the OTCP portal of EPFO . I am not going in details here, but first you need to make sure all the old EPFâs are transferred and linked to the new UAN.Step #2 â In the next step, the EPFO system will automatically identify those UAN for which the EPF transfers have happened and completed. Once they find the idle UAN, they will automatically deactivate that UAN. You donât have to do anything here. This deactivation process will take place from time to time as per decision taken by EPFO. Once the deactivation happens, your old member id (your old EPF accounts) will be linked to new UAN.If you are already sure that your past UAN does not have the EPF linked to them, then you can mail your old UAN number along with recent UAN to your employer and to[emailÂ protected]. They will verify your UANâs status and deactivate the old UAN.How To Merge Two Uan EPF AccountsWhat is UAN?Universal Account Number (UAN) is a unique 12-digit number that is given to each member of the Employeesâ Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO). With the help of the UAN, PF members can easily manage their accounts. The Ministry of Employment and Labour under the guidance of the Government of India issues UAN to PF members. Irrespective of the organisation they work in, all Provided Fund (PF) information can be accessed in one place by PF members with the help of UAN.In earlier days, whenever an individual would join a new organization, he would be given a new PF account number. This made it difficult to keep a check on the updated PF balance. It was also difficult to track activities related to pay change and employees would find it challenging to check PF contribution against the updated pay. To tackle such issues, the UAN was introduced.UAN is a universal number that helps members to gather all the PF accounts linked to multiple IDs of various organizations in one place. By using UAN, the employee can withdraw and also transfer funds in the PF account.More Information on UANâ¢	The UAN is a unique number provided to all employees enrolled for PF benefit. This number is independent of employers and hence does not change even if an employee changes job.â¢	The employer can validate an employee by using his UAN in case KYC documents have been verified.â¢	Since the UAN facility is available online for all employees, no employer can deduct or hold off an employeeâs PF.â¢	An employee can validate the PF deposit made by the employer every month. He/she has to register as an EPF Member on the Portal by using the UAN provided.â¢	EPF passbook access is available through SMS. One can send EPFOHO UAN ENG to 7738299899 from the mobile number that has been registered with the EPFO.How to register the UAN?Here are a few easy steps to be followed for registering the UAN:â¢	Go to the EPF Member Portal.â¢	Click on âActivate UANââ¢	Enter all the information around UAN, such as member id, mobile number, Aadhaar, PAN, name, date of birth and e-mail idâ¢	Select âGet Authorization PINâ to fetch the PIN on the registered mobile numberâ¢	Provide this PIN for verifying the request.â¢	Set up a username and password on the UAN portal for future use.Common Reasons for Allotment of Two UANsIf an employee changes his job, a new EPF account is set up by the new organisation. All existing EPF accounts are auto-linked with the UAN of the employee. Hence, there are high chances that a new UAN is allotted to the employee at the time of moving between jobs. There could be multiple reasons for allotment of new UAN. Listed here are some of the common reasons:â¢	In case an employee has not disclosed his previous UAN â In case an employee changes his job, he must make sure to disclose his existing UAN and EPF account number (Member ID) to the new employer. In absence of disclosure of this information, the employer may open a fresh PF account along with a new UAN.â¢	Non-disclosure of âDate of Exitâ by the previous employer â During the process of EPF transfer to the new employer, the old employer must mention the date of exit in the ECR (Electronic Challan and Return). In case of the absence of this information promptly, the new organisation may allot a new UAN to the employee.Consequences of Holding Two UANsTwo active UANs is not permitted by law and is against the rules. A member must have only one UAN with all the EPF accounts linked to it. EPF accounts cannot be transferred among employees. However, an employee who has two UANs can request for his EPF account to be transferred from one UAN to another and ask his previous UAN to be closed. Thus, an EPF account linked with one UAN will have to be compulsorily transferred to another EPF account linked with a separate UAN.What Should an Employee Do?In recent years, there have been multiple cases of employees assigning different UANs (Universal Account Number) to employees. According to EPF rules, an individual should have only one UAN at any given point of time. The employeeâs EPF account must be linked to his UAN. In case he/she has been assigned two UANs, the previous one must be deactivated at the earliest.Two Methods to Merge Two UAN EPF AccountsEmployees who have been incorrectly allotted two UANs must get one of them deactivated (normally, the previous one). There are two ways of getting the UAN deactivated and the EPF account transferred to the correct and active UAN. Mentioned below are the two commonly used methods:Method 1â¢	Reach out to your employer or EPFO and report the issue at the earliestâ¢	You can write an email to[emailÂ protected]stating about your current and previous UANâ¢	EPFO will begin verification on the issue once it gets notified about the issueâ¢	Your previous UAN is then blocked and the existing UAN remains activeâ¢	After this, you have to submit a claim for transferring the EPF account (linked with the blocked UAN) to the new active account.This process can be time-consuming and the general resolution rate is said to be very low. Thus, EPFO has set up a new procedure which is expected to make things easier for a member. It will especially be helpful while merging two UANs and transferring EPF easily. Here is the new method which can be used by an employee with two UANs:Method 2â¢	After thorough identification, old UAN will be deactivated by EPFO once the transfer of the EPF to the new UAN is completeâ¢	Thus, the old UANs will be blocked automatically and an employeeâs previous member ID will be linked to the new or existing UANâ¢	SMS notification is sent for the deactivation to the employeeâs registered mobile numberâ¢	If the employee has been unable to activate his new UAN, he will be notified to activate it at the earliest to receive the status update of the accountâ¢	There could be instances where the employee gets PF arrears from the previous employer. In such situations, the arrear is credited to the new PF account which is linked with the new UAN.Advantages of UAN for EmployeesMinimum Employer Involvement in PF withdrawals:  With the presence of UAN, the employer involvement is significantly reduced since the PF accumulation from the old organization is auto-transferred to the new PF account after completion of KYC verification.No Need for Fund Transfer: An employee must furnish his UAN details and KYC to the new employer for transferring the old PF balance to the new PF account post verification.Manage via SMS Alerts: Employees will receive SMS as soon as a contribution is made by the employer towards PF. This is provided, the employee has registered on the UAN portal.How to use UAN for PF Transfer?The Employeesâ Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO) constantly takes several measures to make the operation of EPF accounts easier for both the employer and employees. To keep up with the technological advancements, EPFO is constantly striving towards streamlining of processes about online EPF. This is especially applicable to PF transfer and withdrawal of PF which are considered to be tedious and time-consuming processes.EPFO introduced Universal Account Number (UAN), which is the blanket number for multiple Member Ids given to an individual by various employers. UAN allows the linking of multiple EPF Accounts (Member Id) provided to a single EPF member. It offers a range of services such as dynamically updated UAN card, updated PF passbook including all transfer-in details, facility to link previous membersâ ID with present ID, monthly SMS regarding credit of contribution in PF account and facility for auto-triggering transfer request on change of employment.Till recently, PF transfer could be done online by going to the âOnline Transfer Claim Portalâ. However, with the introduction of UAN, the transfer process has been revised and shifted under the âunified portalâ. For online PF transfer, here are some of the important points to note:â¢	An EPF member must have activated his UAN on the UAN portal and the registered mobile number used for activation should be in an active state.â¢	The Bank account number and IFSC code of the employee's bank account must be updated against the UAN. Updated Aadhar number and PAN is not mandatory for PF transfer requests.â¢	The employer must approve the e-KYC for transfer to be executed.â¢	The previous/current employer must have digitally registered authorized signatories on EPFO portal.â¢	PF account number related to previous and current employment of an employee should be updated in EPFO database.â¢	Single transfer requests per member ID can be accepted.FAQs1. What if I have two UAN numbers? Does it impact my EPF balance or transfer in any way?Two different UAN numbers for one employee is not accepted and is against the rules. If you happen to change jobs and move between organizations, you must request for transfer of PF account at the earliest.2. What is the expected timeline for merging two EPF accounts?It normally takes around 20 days from the date of the request to transfer one EPF account to the other.3. Is Form 13 a prerequisite for UAN transfer?Employees working in the corporate sector are required to submit Form 13 for EPF transfer to their new PF account at the time of job change.4. How is Form 13 used?Form 13 is primarily used for the transfer of Provident Fund from one account to another. Employees have to submit this form to their employers, upon which, the latter have to verify and approve the details furnished.

question: I joined the company on 1st November 2022 and have been employedâtwo years of bond which is completed on 31 October 2024. I have given my resignation on 31 August 2024.  Then I am serving my notice period on 15 October I have a request for Work Form Home. They deny the conversation going on and then conversations about the company's work culture so I have said it feels like school while working here. Then they said if you feel like school while working here then we terminate you today(23/10/2024). After 6 days later I received my termination letter. Please guide me on what I can do in this condition.( Surat, Gujarat )
answer: Dear client,1. Review of Employment ContractIt is imperative to thoroughly review your employment contract and any related documents, including the bond agreement you signed upon joining the company. Focus on clauses pertaining to termination, notice periods, and the conditions under which employment may be terminated. Understanding these terms is crucial, as they dictate the legal framework governing your employment relationship. The bond agreement may also contain specific provisions that clarify your obligations upon termination, particularly if you are still within the bonded period.2. Assessment of Termination ValidityExamine the grounds for your termination to ascertain whether they are lawful under applicable labor laws. Most jurisdictions prohibit termination without just cause, especially when an employee is within their notice period. Furthermore, if your termination followed your expression of dissatisfaction regarding the work environment or your request to work from home, it may raise concerns of retaliation. Such retaliation can potentially contravene labor regulations protecting employees from discriminatory or retaliatory termination practices.3. Documentation of EventsIt is essential to maintain comprehensive records of all communications relating to your employment, including any written correspondence and notes from verbal discussions. Documenting conversations that preceded your termination can provide critical evidence if you choose to pursue legal action or a formal complaint. This documentation should include dates, times, and summaries of discussions regarding your resignation, notice period, work-from-home request, and the circumstances surrounding your termination.4. Legal ConsultationConsulting with an employment lawyer is advisable to receive tailored legal advice specific to your situation and jurisdiction. A lawyer can help evaluate the legality of your termination, assess potential claims for wrongful termination or retaliation, and provide guidance on your best course of action. They will analyze the specific details of your case and inform you of your rights under local labor laws, thereby enhancing your understanding of the legal landscape you are navigating.5. Filing a ComplaintDepending on your jurisdiction, you may have the option to file a complaint with a labor board or employment commission regarding your termination. Such bodies often handle disputes related to unfair employment practices and can provide a formal avenue for addressing grievances. Additionally, if your company has an internal grievance procedure, consider utilizing it to contest the termination formally. This process can provide a structured means to present your case and seek redress within the organization.6. Preparation for OutcomesAs you pursue resolution regarding your termination, it is prudent to prepare for various outcomes. Be open to the possibility of negotiating a settlement with your employer, especially if legal counsel advises that this could be beneficial. Simultaneously, begin exploring new employment opportunities to mitigate the impact of your current situation. This dual approach can help ensure you are prepared for both immediate and long-term career prospects.7. Response to TerminationConsider drafting a formal written response to the termination letter, articulating your disagreement with the decision and presenting your perspective on the circumstances leading to your termination. This response can serve to formally document your position and may be shared with your legal counsel. It is essential to convey your concerns clearly and professionally to maintain a record of your objection to the termination.Contact an advocate.

question: I was working in Tech Mahindra, Mumbai and I left it in the month of July 24, in my FFS they are mentioning that FFS is negative because PAN-AADHAAR not being linked together and govt has imposed penalty on them of Rs.  1,04,859/-  which they are now asking me to re-pay this amount to them. question:
I have resigned From Tata Projects limited just after my 3 months service with 10 days short notice out of 90 days. At time of full and final settlement company not considered my served notice period of 10 days and presented a demand of Rs.31815 however i paid this amount.In recepit of my service certificate it is pointed that the reason behind leave the organization mentioned was termination.

What steps i have to take.( Sultanpur, Uttar Pradesh )
answer: Dear Client,For breach of contract of employment on the part of an employee, a company can take action against the employee post-resignation, but cannot mention the reason behind the cessation of employment as termination especially when the employee meets the demands of the company towards breach of contract. The word termination in your relieving letter post-resignation is itself a stigma that adversely affects your future career unless you challenge and nullify that stigma. When you meet the demands of the company, it may be unprofessional and unconstitutional on the part of the Company to issue you a relieving letter placing a stigma on it that infringes a person's fundamental right to life as guaranteed under Article 21 of the Constitution of India. Termination or retrenchment other than a disciplinary action for proven misconduct amounts to illegal termination/retrenchment and is defined as an industrial dispute under Section 2A of the Industrial Dispute Act, 1947 which also violated the mandatory provision of Sec.25F and 25N of the Act that prescribed certain conditions to comply with by the employer before termination/retrenchment of a workman/employee from the employment. In that scenario, the terminated employee/workman serving a legal notice to the Company can raise an industrial dispute before the concerned Labour Commissioner for redressal of the complaint failing which he can approach directly the Industrial Tribunal/Labor Court concerned within one year from termination for adjudication seeking retrenchment compensation under Section 33C(2) of the I D Act provided he is not holding the position of Manager/Supervisor but a workman as defined u/s.2(s) of the Industrial Dispute Act. To restrict IT Companies from exploiting their employees by playing double standards, the Division Bench of the Karnataka High Court in the case of Commissioner of Income Tax v. Texas Instruments India Pvt Ltd (2021) 435 ITR unambiguously held that the IT sector employees considered to be "workmen" under Section 2(s) of the Industrial Dispute Act, 1947. Otherwise, in case you are holding the position of Manager/Administrative Officer in the Company, you have to file a civil suit before the Civil Court seeking appropriate relief in the matter.

question: In the promotion policy of organisation, there is eligibility criteria of promotion to next grade after 4 years. As me and my number of colleagues joined on same duration, same criteria applicable for them. Now even after completion of 5 years, we are not getting promoted. And there is no restriction of vacancies as the work-profile is same. (Also we are playing same roles and responsibilities which taken by already promoted employees to next grade).( Nagpur, Maharashtra )
answer: Dear Client,Regardless of the sector or class of establishments either public or private, the recruitment, promotion, placement, and rationalization of manpower is processed following its standing HR policy and promotion or degradation of manpower is also a prerogative of the management of an establishment. Any complaint or allegation over malpractice or unfair practice against the HR Policy of an establishment shall not be entertained by a Tribunal or Court unless the alleged malpractice or unfairness in HR policy and practice appears on the face of the record. So, it is a very difficult and cumbersome exercise to prove such an allegation against an establishment before the Tribunals/Courts.  Only in case of deviation/ discrimination/mala fide in the policy or rules, if it appears on the face of the record, the Tribunal/High Court may entertain an application or appeal challenging the HR Policy violating the well-established policy of the organization. Otherwise, an application or appeal may be rejected at the stage of admission for lack of merit. So, if you are confident in the merit behind your claim/grievance, you can escalate your grievance before the appropriate authority(Labour Commissioner), State or Central Govt. Labour Courts, SAT/CAT befitting your sector or class of employment for redressal of your grievance.

question:
I was working for a client company through a vendor company ( this company takes care of my Payroll ). Due to some issues I was dropped from my client project and my vendor company asked me to relieve immediately. They didn't ask me to serve notice period in email / call. I have informed them that I was ready to serve notice which they denied. They demanded me to pay 50k which is the travel advance amount I have used for clients' project travel. I was continuously following them up to relieve me for more than a month through email & calls. HR didn't respond to my calls later. Later my email got blocked. At the same time I became bedridden due to pregnancy. They asked me to come to office to talk about relieving formalities. I mentioned my condition clearly and requested them to talk over phone (anyways they were not interested in me serving notice period). No response for email / call from HR. I left it due to my health condition for a while. Now, when I ask them for my relieving documents, they are demanding me to pay three months salary and accusing me of not serving notice which I was ready to. 
What should I do in this case? I have mentioned clearly I was ready to serve in other projects but they terminated me and also denied me to serve any notice.
Now they are blocking my experience letter / relieving documents.
The company didn't pay any compensation to me for immediate termination. Can someone help me how to proceed on this further?( Tiruchirappalli, Tamil Nadu )
answer: Dear Client,Termination or dismissal other than a disciplinary action for proven misconduct amounts to illegal termination/ retrenchment and is defined as an industrial dispute under Section 2A of the Industrial Dispute Act, 1947 which also violated the mandatory provision of Sec.25F and 25N of the I D Act that prescribed certain conditions to comply with by the employer before termination/retrenchment of a workman/employee from the employment. Any Termination of a workman is covered under the Industrial Disputes Act and it falls under âRetrenchmentâ. In the case of Punjab Land Development Corporation Vs Labour Court, 1990 (II) LLJ, 70 SC, the Supreme Court held that The expression âretrenchmentâ is not to be understood in its narrow, natural and contextual meaning, but is to be understood in its wider, literal meaning to mean termination of service of a workman for any reason whatsoever. Further, in the case of Santosh Gupta Vs State Bank of Patiala AIR 1980 SC 1219, the Supreme Court ruled that the expression retrenchment must include every termination of the services of a workman by an act of the employer. Under Chapters V-A & V-B of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947, for retrenchment of a workman of an industrial establishment employing below 100 workmen, an employer has to serve one month's notice or wages in lieu of notice. Even as per Clause 13(1) of the model Standing Order under Industrial Employment(Standing Orders) Act, 1946, for terminating the employment of a permanent workman, notice in writing shall be given either by the employer or the workman one month's notice in the case of monthly rated workmen and two weeks' notice in the case of other workmen; one month's or two week's pay, as the case may be, may be paid in lieu of notice. In that scenario, the terminated employee/workman can raise an industrial dispute before the concerned Labour Commissioner for redressal of the complaint failing which he can approach directly the Industrial Tribunal/Labor Court concerned for adjudication provided he is not holding the position of Manager/Supervisor but a workman as defined u/s.2(s) of the Industrial Dispute Act. Otherwise, in case he is holding the position of Manager/Administrative Officer in the Company, he has to file a civil suit before the Civil Court seeking appropriate relief in the matter. If you are an employee of the IT Company then be informed that to restrict IT Companies from exploiting their employees by playing double standards, the Division Bench of the Karnataka High Court in the case of Commissioner of Income Tax v. Texas Instruments India Pvt Ltd (2021) 435 ITR unambiguously held that the IT sector employees considered to be "workmen" under Section 2(s) of the Industrial Dispute Act, 1947.

question: How can I recover my cash lost by online job scammer( Alappuzha, Kerala )
answer: Dear Client,The National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal(NCCRP) is an initiative of the Government of India to facilitate victims/complainants to report cybercrime including online job scams or complaints. question: I am an intern and frequently i've been getting my payment extremely late due to which my monthly budget schedule shakes up. I continuously msg for updates of payment but get no reply. Is it possible to take any legal action regarding this?( Pune, Maharashtra )
answer: Dear Client,Internships are often unpaid and may not lead to a full-time job. Stipends are provided to those ineligible to receive a regular salary or wage in return for their services. Researchers, graduate students, clergy, interns and apprentices are common recipients. However, internships remain an unregulated sector and as a result, in most cases, interns are not legally entitled to minimum wages or modes of legal redressal that otherwise apply to permanent employees. So considering the status of interns, in the absence of a specific stipulation in your offer letter, your claim for payment of a stipend in the scheduled time may not be upheld even through litigation.

question:

My father worked in a co-op housing society as a guard  from the last 9-10 years.

answer: Dear Client,The Office of the Housing Society is not considered a commercial establishment as defined under the state-specific Shops and Establishment Act and as such no social security laws or labour laws are applicable to the employees engaged by the housing society for the purpose of maintenance of common facilities to residents of the housing society. The Honâble Supreme Court, in the case of âManagement of Som Vihar Apartment Owners Housing Maintenance Society Ltd. v. Workmen C/o Indian Engineering And General Mazdoor,(2) while considering the applicability of Industrial Disputes Act, 1947 to the Apartment Owners Housing Society formed by the Apartment Owners, has held that when personal services are rendered to the Members of a Society and that Society is constituted only for the purposes of those Members to engage the services of such employees, its activity should not be treated as an industry nor are they workmen. The Apartment Owners Association is an Association created for the benefit of the Members of the Association and the so-called workmen employed by the Association are rendering only personal services to the Members of the Association. As aforesaid, to attract the provisions of the Act, essential ingredients of an âestablishmentâ as set out in section 2(e) of the Act which contemplates that the activities must be commercial in nature, carried on by the office or Department of the Government or the Local Authority must be satisfied. So, as the housing society is not considered a commercial establishment and also in view of the above averments of the Apex Court, employees engaged by the society are not entitled to claim the benefit of social security laws from the Housing Society.

question: Sir, I have mailed my resignation letter to my HR on 19th august and joined another company on 20 th august. But still my previous employer paid me full salary for august. On 9 September I contacted my HR regarding this issue. They said your last working day would be on 3 September as my immediate manager accepted my separation from organization on 3 September.  So in this case what should I do.( Pune, Maharashtra )
answer: Dear Client,Before joining another Company you are required to tender your resignation and to obtain a relieving letter from the earlier company serving the notice period as per the terms of employment that eventually caused the overlapping of service. The overlapping in service in respect of previous and present establishment and any anomaly or discrepancy in EPF records of any registered member may be a ground for future dispute. When your EPF record shows an anomaly in the joining and exit date in both the previous and present Company which is contradictory, then until and unless those anomalies are rectified by the concerned employers, PF records will show overlapping or dual employment. A joint declaration form is used to correct Provident Fund (PF) member details. It is a combined form that the employee and employer sign and submit to the regional PF commissioner to update the wrong information entered in the employeesâ PF accounts. An employee cannot update the service history. Only an employer can rectify the error in the employment record of the EPFO. So if an employee finds an error in the database, he should contact their present or previous employers and get it corrected. In the given situation, to resolve the issue of overlapping in the P F records of both employers, you need to approach the office of the Regional P F Commissioner who is the competent authority to resolve any anomaly arising out of the date of appointment and date of discharge in EPF records. An individual can file a complaint using the EPF i-Grievance Management System (www. https://epfigms.gov.in/). Once you succeed in wiping out the stigma of dual employment from your EPF records with the cooperation of your previous and present employer, your scope of employment with other companies will be restored with clean employment records. In case of non-cooperation from both previous and current employers which amounted to unfair labour practice, you may bring the matter to the notice of the Regopmal PF Commissioner and the concerned Labour Commissioner or Asst. Labour Commissioner/LEO/Chief Inspector(Shops and Establishment) for a resolution in the matter.

question: How to remove or change this DOE of previous employers ?( Pune, Maharashtra )
answer: Dear Client,A joint declaration form(JDF) is used to correct Provident Fund (PF) member details. If the complaint is not resolved even on receipt of JDF, you can approach the Employeesâ Provident Funds Appellate Tribunal (EPFAT) which was constituted under the provisions of the Section 7 D of the EPF and M P Act 1952, Now, as per the Finance Act 2017, the Employees' Provident Fund Appellate Tribunal has been merged with Central Government Industrial Tribunal w.e.f. 26.05.2017. question: can i re-join my job after maternity leave (approx one year leave).i sent the letter to the department after one year of maternity leave dt.20/03/2017 but till date they have not given any approval to join( Jamshedpur, Jharkhand )

question: Can we submit the EWS certificate from parents for a married woman in our Telangana?( Siddipet, Telangana )

answer: Dear Client,Regardless of the sector or character of establishments either public or private, the recruitment of manpower is processed following its standing recruitment policy and recruitment of manpower is also a prerogative of the establishment. When I joined the current company I got to know that my previous company didn't want me to join this organisation because they have some agreement that I shouldn't join some companies that are clients to them in the past. I am not aware of this and explained the current company. They said, it won't be an issue and I joined the company but now my previous company saying in future background checks they will say contract breached. What should I do now?

Do I need to worry about this, if I want to change the company in future?( Hyderabad, Telangana )
answer: Dear Client,Section 27 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872 prohibits any agreement/contract in restraint of trade and profession. The law states that an agreement or employment contract will be illegal only if it restrains someone from exercising a lawful profession/ trade/ business. As per the mandate of Section 27, any terms and conditions of an agreement that directly or indirectly compels the employee to serve the employer or puts a restriction on them joining the competitor or other employer are not valid and are to be void on contest. The employee has the right to resign from the employment for a better opportunity, even if there is a non-compete clause in the contract of employment or if he/she has agreed to serve the employer for a specific period under a service bond. In the case where the employer can prove that the employee is joining the competitor to disclose the trade secret then the court may issue an injunction order restricting the employee from joining the competitor. Further, Section 73 of the Act makes provision for un-liquidated damages (not stipulated in a contract), Section 74 deals with liquidated damages (stipulated in a contract), and no compensation is attracted for mere breach of contract u/s.73. 74 of the Act unless such breach resulted in an actual loss or damage to the opposite party employer. Background verification (BGV) check is a process many organizations carry out to verify the information provided by the candidate during hiring. Verification of EPFO records through UAN is critical for conducting employee background checks because it allows employers to confirm that their employees are not using false or stolen identities to gain employment. In case of a negative background verification check an employer can even reject/terminate the employment of the candidate and that will potentially damage your service career. So, receiving the threat or warning from the previous employer to damage your background verification check putting a stigma of breach of contract which apparently proves the unfair labour practice of the employer, can be challenged by invoking Section 27 read with Sections 73 & 74 of the Indian Contract Act. in the given scenario, serving a strong legal notice to the previous employer who adopted unfair labour practice to damage the career of an ex-employee, reach out to the office of the concerned State Labour Commissioner or the office of the Chief Inspector, Shops and Establishments, as the case may be, to file a complaint against the company over alleged unfair labour practice for redressal of your grievance, provided you are a workman as defined under Sec.2(s) of the Industrial Dispute Act, 1947.  But, if you are holding the position of Manager or Administrator in the Company, you have to file a civil suit against the Company before the Civil Court seeking desired relief in the matter. If required, reach out to an Advocate experienced in service matters for guidance and steps. Be informed that to restrict IT Companies from exploiting their employees by playing double standards, the Division Bench of the Karnataka High Court in the case of Commissioner of Income Tax v. Texas Instruments India Pvt Ltd (2021) 435 ITR unambiguously held that the IT sector employees considered to be "workmen" under Section 2(s) of the Industrial Dispute Act, 1947. Further, the Hon'ble Bombay High Court in the case of Godrej and Boyce Manufacturing Company Ltd. v. Shivkranti Kamgar Sanghatana, 2024 SCC OnLine Bom 938, decided on 28-03-2024 ruled out that the nature of duties and functions is the determining factor in ascertaining âworkmanâ under S. 2(s) of Industrial Disputes Act, 1947.
