question: My sons current employer have his original certificates in custody and are demanding 2 lakhs to return them of he wants to quit. They have taken undertaki gduring his joining. Is it legally correct? What steps do we take now?( Tiruchirappalli, Tamil Nadu )
answer: Dear Client,A service/employment bond itself does not create any relationship between an employer and an employee unless and until it is followed by the essential steps required to make the Bond valid and enforceable under the law. The validity of Employment bonds can be challenged based on Section 27 of the Indian Contract Act,1872 which prohibits any agreement in restraint of trade and profession. The law states that an agreement (employment bond) will be illegal only if it restrains someone from exercising a lawful profession/ trade/ business. As per the mandate of Section 27 of the Indian Contract Act,1872, any terms and conditions of an agreement that directly or indirectly compels the employee to serve the employer or puts a restriction on them joining the competitor or other employer is not valid. The employee has the right to resign from the employment even if he has agreed to the employment bond to serve the employer for a specific period. In the case where the employer can prove that the employee is joining the competitor to disclose the trade secret then the court may issue an injunction order restricting the employee from joining the competitor. Further, Section 73 of the Act makes provision for un-liquidated damages (not stipulated in a contract), Section 74 deals with liquidated damages (stipulated in a contract) and no compensation is attracted for mere breach of contract u/s.73. 74 of the Act unless such breach resulted in an actual loss or damage to the opposite party employer. Further, withholding your original documents on the cessation of the relationship between an employer and employee post-resignation to recover the bond value amounts to unfair labour practice on the part of the employer in view of the aforesaid provision of the Indian Contract Act,1872.  So, in the prevailing situation, if you are not holding a position of manager or supervisor in the Company, but a workman as defined under Sec.2(s) of the Industrial Dispute Act, 1947. serving a legal notice to the Company reach out to the office of the concerned Labour Commissioner or the Chief Inspector, Shops and Establishment to file a complaint against the company over alleged unfair labour practice for redressal of your grievance, But, if you are holding the position of Manager or Administrator in the Company, you have to file a civil suit before the Civil Court for desired relief in the matter.

But denial or withholding of F & F dues, relieving letters, and other documents of employee post acceptance of his/her resignation is considered unfair labour practices on the part of the employer. Section 27 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872 states that an agreement or employment contract will be illegal only if it restrains someone from exercising a lawful profession/ trade/ business. As per the mandate of Section 27, any terms and conditions of an agreement that directly or indirectly compels the employee to serve the employer or puts a restriction on them joining the competitor or other employer are not valid and are to be void on contest. The employee has the right to resign from the employment for a better opportunity, even if there is a non-compete clause in the contract of employment or if he/she has agreed to serve the employer for a specific period under a service bond. question: Dear Sir, is it mandatory for every company to provide mediclaim to all employees who receives salary above 21000 per month? In this case, can the company deduct the insurance premium from the employees take home salary?( Bangalore, Karnataka )

However, after submitting my resignation, the company informed me that Iâm not eligible to resign, claiming itâs only been two days since my training ended, although they were making me do the same work during that time as I am doing right now. They are refusing to allow me to serve my notice period and have also said they wonât pay me for the days Iâve worked. They're basically forcing me to continue working for them for one more month and then send my resignation and serve my notice period or to leave right away without any pay.

I find this treatment deeply unfair and concerning, and I would appreciate any advice or guidance you may have regarding my rights in this situation.( Guwahati, Assam )
answer: Dear Client,From the contents of your query appears that the company is itself in default while issuing an appointment letter showing no specified exit policy and such an arbitrary action can amount to unfair labour practice as defined under Section 2(ra) of the Industrial Dispute Act, 1947. However, even if any arbitrary and unjustified action is taken by the employer that can be challenged by invoking Section 27 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872 which prohibits any agreement/contract in restraint of trade and profession. The law states that an agreement or employment contract will be illegal only if it restrains someone from exercising a lawful profession/ trade/ business. As per the mandate of Section 27, any terms and conditions of an agreement that directly or indirectly compels the employee to serve the employer or puts a restriction on them joining the competitor or other employer are not valid and are to be void on contest. The employee has the right to resign from the employment for a better opportunity, even if there is a non-compete clause in the contract of employment or if he/she has agreed to serve the employer for a specific period under a service bond. In the case where the employer can prove that the employee is joining the competitor to disclose the trade secret then the court may issue an injunction order restricting the employee from joining the competitor. Further, Section 73 of the Act makes provision for un-liquidated damages (not stipulated in a contract), Section 74 deals with liquidated damages (stipulated in a contract), and no compensation is attracted for mere breach of contract u/s.73. 74 of the Act unless such breach resulted in an actual loss or damage to the opposite party employer. Regardless of reasons, on cessation of employment, an employee is entitled to an experience certificate, relieving letter and F & F settlement dues from the employer within 30 days of the last working days (LWD) and denial of which amounted to unfair labour practices. So, in the prevailing situation, if you are not holding a position of manager or supervisor in the Company, but a workman as defined under Sec.2(s) of the Industrial Dispute Act, 1947. serving a legal notice to the Company reach out to the office of the concerned Labour Commissioner or the office of the Chief Inspector, Shops and Establishments, as the case may be, to file a complaint against the company over alleged unfair labour practice for redressal of your grievance, But, if you are holding the position of Manager or Administrator in the Company, you have to file a civil suit against the Company before the Civil Court seeking desired relief in the matter. question: My employer repeatedly demands original marksheet of class 10th. The company is not registered and they deduct 10% tds from everyone's salary. At the time of salary they didn't give salary slip to any employee.( Bangalore, Karnataka )
answer: Dear Client,An employer can neither demand an original mark sheet from a candidate/employee nor keep it in their custody as a token of security. A self-attested Xerox copy of the mark sheet or a copy attested by any gazetted officer of the state or central government is sufficient to meet any purpose. A salary slip contains a detailed break-up of an employee's salary from gross salary to the take-home salary with deductions. A salary slip is a legal right of an employee in a company and if the company refuses to provide a salary slip or pay slip, it amounts to unfair labour practice. TAN (Tax Deduction and Collection Account Number) is mandatory for any company, firm, or individual, who deducts or collects tax at source, on behalf of the Income Tax Department. As per Section 192 of the Income Tax Act, 1961, TDS is required to be deducted from all the monetary amounts paid by the employer under the head 'Salary' to his employee if the amount so paid exceeds the threshold exemption limit of Income. Form 16 is a TDS certificate issued by the employer as proof of tax deducted from the employee's salary income. It serves as proof that tax has been deducted at source from the employee's salary income and deposited with the government. It is essential for filing income tax returns. A taxpayer can download Form 16 from TRACES (TDS Reconciliation Analysis and Correction Enabling System) an online website of the Income Tax Department of India. As explained in the query, all the actions of the company appear to be arbitrary and unfair labour practices as defined under Section 2(ra) of the Industrial Dispute Act. So, you can make a complaint/grievance against the company before the concerned Labour Commissioner of the State Govt. who is the appropriate authority under the Payment of Wages Act, Shops and Establishments Act and Minimum Wages Act to resolve the dispute.

question: Hi, i put down my resign on 18 sept and my company wants to terminate me on 24th sept with the allegations that on 6th sept during client call i was involved in sexual activity. Now i have been denied of my notice period benefits.( Jaipur, Rajasthan )
answer: Dear Client,An employee is an employee even during the notice period post-resignation and the employer can take action against him for the commission of misconduct as per the company's policy/service rules. However, an employer cannot terminate his service without conducting an inquiry into the allegation and not allowing the delinquent employee to defend his case before the inquiry committee which is considered a violation of the principle of natural justice and a violation of the provision of laws of the land. Termination or retrenchment other than a disciplinary action for proven misconduct amounts to illegal termination/retrenchment and is defined as an industrial dispute under Section 2A of the Industrial Dispute Act, 1947 which also violated the mandatory provision of Sec.25F and 25N of the Act that prescribed certain conditions to comply with by the employer before termination/retrenchment of a workman/employee from the employment. In that scenario, the terminated employee/workman can raise an industrial dispute before the concerned Labour Commissioner for redressal of the complaint failing which he can approach directly the Industrial Tribunal/Labor Court concerned within one year from termination for adjudication seeking reinstatement or retrenchment compensation under Section 33C(2) of the I D Act provided he is not holding the position of Manager/Supervisor but a workman as defined u/s.2(s) of the Industrial Dispute Act. If you belong to the IT sector company, be informed that to restrict IT Companies from exploiting their employees by playing double standards, the Division Bench of the Karnataka High Court in the case of Commissioner of Income Tax v. Texas Instruments India Pvt Ltd (2021) 435 ITR unambiguously held that the IT sector employees considered to be "workmen" under Section 2(s) of the Industrial Dispute Act, 1947. Otherwise, in case you are holding the position of Manager/Administrative Officer in the Company, you have to file a civil suit before the Civil Court seeking appropriate relief in the matter.

answer: Dear Client,Usually show cause notice is issued to the delinquent employee under the signature of the Disciplinary Authority appointing therein the Inquiry Officer and the presenting officer to conduct the inquiry into the allegation and submit a report to the Disciplinary Authority for awarding punishment based on the IO's report and applicable of code of punishment. However, as per DOPT OM dated 26/03/2024 and Rule 14(2) of the CCS (CCA) Rules, 1965, clause 2.2.1, whenever the disciplinary authority is of the opinion that there are grounds for inquiring into the truth of any imputation of misconduct or misbehavior against a Government servant, it may itself inquire into, or appointed under this rule or under the provisions of the Public Servants (Inquiries) Act, 1850, as the case may be, an authority to inquire into the truth thereof. There is no bar to the immediate superior officer holding an inquiry but, as a rule, the person who undertakes this task should not be suspected of any bias in such cases. According to DOPT OM dated 28/03/2013, the provision of FR 17(1) stipulates that an officer who is absent from duty without any authority shall not be entitled to any pay and allowances during the period of such absence. However, in case of any injustice, an aggrieved employee can approach the concerned bench of the Central Administrative Tribunal(CAT) by filing an application in Form - I under sub-rule 1 Rule 4 of the Central Administrative Tribunal (Procedure) Rules, 1987 seeking appropriate relief in the matter and if the CAT passes any adverse order, you can challenge the order through an appeal before the High Court seeking appropriate relief based on the merit of the dispute.

question: I want to join next company with serving 30 days of notice period but my current employer not releasing me before 90 days of serving notice period.( Pune, Maharashtra )
answer: Dear Client,An employer cannot force an employee to complete his notice period post-resignation to deprive him avail of a better opportunity that amounts to unfair labour practice. In the absence of any specific stipulation in the contract of employment/appointment letter or any buy-back policy, an employer can deduct the payment on a pro-rata basis toward the unserved period of notice post-resignation, but cannot withhold the relieving letter, experience certificate or payment full and final settlement of an outgoing employee. Section 27 of the Indian Contract Act, of 1872, states that any terms and conditions of an agreement that directly or indirectly compels the employee to serve the employer or puts a restriction on them joining the competitor or other employer is not valid. An employee has the right to resign from the employment even if he has agreed to serve the employer for a specific period.  In the case where the employer can prove that the employee is joining the competitor to disclose the trade secret then the court may issue an injunction order restricting the employee from joining the competitor. So, in the prevailing situation, if you are not holding the position of Manager/Supervisor but a workman as defined u/s.2(s) of the Industrial Dispute Act then after serving a legal notice to the Company, reach out to the office of the concerned Labour Commissioner for filing a complaint against the employer over alleged unfair labour practice to resolve the grievance. But, if you were holding the position of Manager or Administrator in the Company, you have to file a civil suit before the Civil Court for desired relief in the matter.

question: Workers  working 10years, 15years on Ftc(fixed time contact) renewaling for every two years, but not regularising. No service  brake  is .can we appeal ?( Hyderabad, Telangana )
answer: Dear Client,Fixed-term contractual employment is regulated by the Contract Labour( Regulation & Abolition Act,1970,  the Industrial Employment (Standing Orders) Act, 1946 (SO Act) and the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947 (IDA) which are the three main federal laws that govern working conditions for âworkmenâ (that is, excluding employees in managerial, supervisory, and administrative positions). However, courts have held that fixed-term employees or temporary employees must be hired only for projects that are temporary or to serve as temporary replacements. Section 10 of the Contract Labour(R & A) Act, 1970 prohibits the engagement of contractual workers in the permanent perennial nature of jobs in an establishment. Engaging workmen on a Fixed Term Contract basis for permanent positions (that is, not for a temporary project) is construed as an unfair labour practice and violation of Contract labour(R & A) Act.  If a Court/Tribunal finds an individual to be a de facto permanent employee (that is, not a fixed-term employee), the individual is entitled to all salary and benefits as provided to permanent employees and other benefits linked to continuous service. Though the recent amendment to the Standing Order Act permits appointments of fixed-term contractual employment across all industries, employing someone indefinitely for such a long period of 10/15 years can be questioned and may be construed that they were engaged against the permanent perennial nature of jobs in the establishment. The Supreme Court, vide its judgement dated March 12, 2024, in the case of Mahanadi Coalfields Limited v. Brajrajnagar Coal Mines Workersâ Union [Civil Appeal No(s). 4092-4093/2024], has held that the workers who are engaged in the performance of work which is perennial or permanent in nature would not be classified as contractual workers. Given the proposition of relevant laws and the verdict of the Apex Court on the subject, you may escalate your grievance or demand for regularisation in the establishment before the concerned appropriate authority and judicial authority i.e, Labour Commissioner or State/Central Industrial Tribunal seeking your regularisation in the establishment.

question: Gratuity not paying, vda /minimum wage increase,  not paid by contractor,  principal employer is responsibility  is there  or not( Hyderabad, Telangana )
answer: Dear Client,Under the Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972, Gratuity is payable if an organization employs 10 or more individuals on a single day in the preceding 12 months are liable to pay gratuity. An employee, contractual worker, or temporary individual has to work for at least 5 continuous years to be eligible for gratuity. This also includes service that is interrupted due to leave, accident, sickness, lockout, strike, layoff, termination of work not caused by the employee, and absence from duty without leave. If the contractor fails to discharge his liability of payment of gratuity to the eligible worker, the principal employer of the establishment is liable for payment of gratuity and other dues to the contractor workers. question:

Unless the said discrepancy is rectified by the ex-employer, the employee's EPF record will reflect the discrepancy that may potentially affect his contribution and claim from the fund. A joint declaration form(JDF) is used to correct Provident Fund (PF) member details. It is a combined form that the employee and employer jointly sign and submit to the regional PF commissioner to update the wrong information entered in the employeesâ PF accounts by default. In the given situation, to resolve the issue of wrong or incorrect entry in the P F records of the previous employer who uploaded the reason of exit from employment as death, you need to approach the office of the Regional P F Commissioner who is the competent authority to resolve any anomaly/discrepancy arising out of date of appointment and date of exit of an employee in EPF records. For lack of cooperation from the employers who are duty-bound to correct the records of member employees in EPF records despite receipt of JDF, an individual can file a complaint using the EPF i-Grievance Management System (www. https://epfigms.gov.in/). or filing a complaint offline in the office of the Regional PF Commissioner concerned. If the complaint is not resolved at the level of Regl. PF Commissioner, you can approach the Employeesâ Provident Funds Appellate Tribunal (EPFAT) which was constituted under the provisions of Section 7 D of the EPF and M P Act 1952, Now, as per the Finance Act 2017, the Employees' Provident Fund Appellate Tribunal has been merged with Central Government Industrial Tribunal w.e.f. 26.05.2017. So, if no relief yields from the office of the Regl. PF Commissioner, you may approach the Central Government Industrial Tribunal for appropriate relief.

question: 1.5year ago i got a job in district court of tripura as a PA stenographer with 2800 grade pay and i had applied NOC for the same post for state public service as PA stenographer with 2800 grade pay and my prayer has accepted and they had given me the NOC from my parent department. There is a rule for NOC that for the same grade pay no department can give NOC but my parent department given me NOC. No after serving 1.5years in court as PA i have technically resigned and joined in another state govt department 2months ago. So i want to go back my parents department i.e. in court. My question is this can i file a case against my parent department that why they gave me NOC for the same post with same grade pay?( Agartala, Tripura )
answer: Dear Client,As per law, an employee cannot rejoin the same job, once his or her resignation is accepted, because when the resignation is accepted, the relationship between the employee and employer gets seized/severed. As per the Ministry of Finance Office Memo No. 3379-E.III (B)/65 dated the 17th June, 1965, the resignation is treated as a technical resignation where a Government servant has applied through proper channels for a post in the same or some other Department and is on selection, required to resign the previous post for administrative reasons. The resignation will be treated as technical resignation if these conditions are met, even if the Government servant has not mentioned the word âTechnicalâ while submitting his resignation. The benefit of past service, if otherwise admissible under rules, may be given in such cases. Resignation in other cases including where competent authority has not allowed the Government servant to forward the application through proper channels will not be treated as a technical resignation and the benefit of past service will not be admissible. The benefit of past service is allowed in such cases subject to the fulfillment of the following conditions: (i) the Government servant should intimate the details of such application immediately on their joining; (ii) the Government servant at the time of resignation should specifically make a request, indicating that he is resigning to take up another appointment under the Government for which he applied before joining the Government service; (iii) the authority accepting the resignation should satisfy itself that had the employee been in service on the date of application for the post mentioned by the employee, his application would have been forwarded through proper channel. As per DOPT's OM dated 24/11/2022, a Government servant acquiring a lien on a post will cease to hold any lien previously acquired on any other post. A permanent Government servant appointed in another Central Government Department/Office/ State Government has to resign from his parent department unless he reverts to that department within a period of 2 years, or 3 years. An undertaking to abide by this condition may be taken from him at the time of forwarding his application to other departments/offices. Being the position as stated above you may seek further clarification on the subject from the concerned Deptt (DOPT) or apply to the State Administrative Tribunal (SAT) constituted under the Administrative Tribunal Act, 1985. But before approaching SAT, you have to represent your grievance before the HOD concerned and if your grievance is not resolved or you are aggrieved with the reply of the HOD to your grievance, you can apply before the concerned Bench of the State Administrative Tribunal(SAT) following the procedure as prescribed under the State Administrative Tribunal (Procedure) Rules. If required, you may hire the service of an Advocate handling SAT matters to navigate the issue in the right way.

question: I was working as a mechanical fitter in cement factory which is a private sector company and last month i got retired by the company at the age of 58. I want to claim my 2 years of salary from the company because in my knowledge supreme court has said the retirement age for the private company employee will be 60. Please guide me for the same.( Satna, Madhya Pradesh )
answer: Dear Client,There is no official retirement age in private sector companies. However, employees can retire at the age of 58 or 60 based on their employment contract, employerâs policies, or mutual agreement with the employer. The retirement age for private company employees who belong to I T Sector, Multinational Companies MNC, and Banking Sector is 60 years, and for Marketing Sectors is between 58 to 60 years. Clause 3 of Schedule - I B of the Industrial Employment (Standing Orders) Act, 1946 states that the age of retirement or superannuation of a workman shall be as may be agreed upon between the employer and the workman under an agreement or as specified in a settlement or award which is binding on both the workman and the employer. Where there is no such agreed age, retirement or superannuation shall be on completion of 58 years of age by the workman. In G.M. Talang and Ors. V/s Shaw Wallace and Co. and Anr., as decided on 24.03.1964 the Honâble Supreme Court of India held that after taking into consideration the views of the earlier Committees and Commissions including those of the Second Pay Commission the report of which has been released recently, we feel that the retirement age for workmen in all industries should be fixed at 60. Accordingly, the norm for retirement age is fixed at 60. The above judgment was upheld in Tej Bahadur Ram V/s State of U.P. and Ors, arising from SLP(C)No.18692/2005. In the case of employees who are not workmen, the age of retirement is decided by the service rules determined by the Company and accepted by the Company. In the case of managerial cadre or executives, the age of retirement is determined by the contract of employment/employment agreement. So, if there is no employment contract, employerâs policies, mutual agreement with the employer, or a settlement award governing the age of retirement, you may take up the matter with the Company as well as the Labour Commissioner or, Inspector of Factories for the review of your retirement age, otherwise, the provision of Clause 3 of Schedule - I B of the Industrial Employment (Standing Orders) Act, 1946 prescribed fixing the age of retirement at 58 shall prevail.

question: I am working in a Pvt Ltd Biotechnology company & signed a bond for 5 years. But the work pressure & environment is so toxic and painful. Even I am forced to work everyday approximately 10-12 hours which includes holidays & weekly offs since 1.8 years. When I have resigned recently, they are not ready to relive me and asked me that they have trained me on work and I can's leave. However as a experienced person I haven't learned a single new thing from this organization whereas I have trained their fresher to work properly. What is the legal rights for me to sue the company and get relieve smoothly ?( Bhubaneswar, Orissa )
answer: Dear Client,A service/employment bond itself does not create any relationship between an employer and an employee unless and until it is followed by the essential steps required to make the Bond valid and enforceable under the law. The validity of Employment bonds can be challenged based on Section 27 of the Indian Contract Act,1872 which prohibits any agreement in restraint of trade and profession. The law states that an agreement (employment bond) will be illegal only if it restrains someone from exercising a lawful profession/ trade/ business. As per the mandate of Section 27 of the Indian Contract Act,1872, any terms and conditions of an agreement that directly or indirectly compels the employee to serve the employer or puts a restriction on them joining the competitor or other employer is not valid. The employee has the right to resign from the employment even if he has agreed to the employment bond to serve the employer for a specific period. In the case where the employer can prove that the employee is joining the competitor to disclose the trade secret then the court may issue an injunction order restricting the employee from joining the competitor. Further, Section 73 of the Act makes provision for un-liquidated damages (not stipulated in a contract), Section 74 deals with liquidated damages (stipulated in a contract) and no compensation is attracted for mere breach of contract u/s.73. 74 of the Act unless such breach resulted in an actual loss or damage to the opposite party employer. So, in the prevailing situation, if you are not holding a position of manager or supervisor in the Company, but a workman as defined under Sec.2(s) of the Industrial Dispute Act, 1947. serving a legal notice to the Company reach out to the office of the concerned Labour Commissioner or the Chief Inspector, Shops and Establishment to file a complaint against the company over alleged unfair labour practice for redressal of your grievance, But, if you are holding the position of Manager or Administrator in the Company, you have to file a civil suit before the Civil Court for desired relief in the matter.

A joint declaration form(JDF) is used to correct Provident Fund (PF) member details. It is a combined form that the employee and employer jointly sign and submit to the regional PF commissioner to update the wrong information entered in the employeesâ PF accounts by default. question: I was working for a Jaipur based private company and was employed at the udaipur Location. In my pocket my cellphone Was unlocked and by mistake the call was connected to my manager as he was the last person I called. Me and my friends were having some alcohol and doing conversation about my work life balance and sharing my frustrations and my manager kept the call on for 1 and a half hour and recorded everything. And based on that conversation I was fired. Is it legal and also it's been more then 17 days they are not responding to my sms about F&F( Udaipur, Rajasthan )
answer: Dear Client,The ground of firing from service is unacceptable and impermissible under the law and amounts to unfair labour practices on the part of the employer. Termination or dismissal other than a disciplinary action for proven misconduct amounts to illegal termination/retrenchment and is defined as an industrial dispute under Section 2A of the Industrial Dispute Act, 1947 which also violated the mandatory provision of Sec.25F and 25N of the Act that prescribed certain mandatory conditions to comply with by the employer before termination/retrenchment of a workman/employee from the employment. In that scenario, the terminated employee/workman can raise an industrial dispute before the concerned State Labour Commissioner or the Chief Inspector, Shops and Establishment for redressal of the complaint failing which he can approach directly the State Industrial Tribunal/Labor Court concerned for adjudication of the dispute provided he is not holding the position of Manager/Supervisor but a workman as defined u/s.2(s) of the Industrial Dispute Act. Additionally, he can file an application under Section 33C(2) of the I D Act before the Labour Court claiming dues and compensation admissible under the Act post-illegal termination from the employment. Otherwise, in case he is holding the position of Manager/Administrative Officer in the Company, he has to file a civil suit before the Civil Court seeking appropriate relief in the matter.

An employee could be entitled to get 'payment in lieu of notice'. This means the employer stops work straight away but still gets paid for their notice period. Termination or dismissal other than a disciplinary action for proven misconduct amounts to illegal termination/ retrenchment and is defined as an industrial dispute under Section 2A of the Industrial Dispute Act, 1947 which also violated the mandatory provision of Sec.25F and 25N of the I D Act that prescribed certain conditions to comply with by the employer before termination/retrenchment of a workman/employee from the employment. Under Chapters V-A & V-B of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947, for retrenchment of a workman of an industrial establishment employing below 100 workmen, an employer has to pay one month's notice or wages in lieu of notice, compensation of Fifteen days average pay for every completed year of service. 6 months and above to be treated as one year and service of Notice to the appropriate Government(Labour Commissioner) informing retrenchment of workmen. In that scenario, serving a legal notice to the Company, the terminated employee/workman can raise an industrial dispute before the concerned Labour Commissioner for redressal of the dispute failing which he can approach directly the Industrial Tribunal/Labor Court concerned for adjudication of the dispute provided he is not holding the position of Manager/Supervisor but a workman as defined u/s.2(s) of the Industrial Dispute Act. To restrict IT Companies from exploiting their employees by playing double standards, the Division Bench of the Karnataka High Court in the case of Commissioner of Income Tax v. Texas Instruments India Pvt Ltd (2021) 435 ITR unambiguously held that the IT sector employees considered to be "workmen" under Section 2(s) of the Industrial Dispute Act, 1947. If required you can hire the service of an Advocate experienced in service matters to navigate the issue in the right way.

question:
Hi,
I hope you're doing well. I have a question regarding gratuity eligibility:
I have worked with a private organization for around 16 years. However, for the past 15 years, the salary payments were made in cash, and I only have a salary statement for the last year. The company is relatively small, with about 15 to 20 employees.
I joined as a fresher in 2003, so my documentation is limited that time and the i have only salary statement for the last year. Given this situation, am I still eligible for a gratuity amount?
Any guidance or advice would be greatly appreciated!( Chennai, Tamil Nadu )
answer: Dear Client,An organization/establishment with a workforce of 10 individuals and above is liable to pay gratuity under the Payment of Gratuity Act 1972. A gratuity must be paid to an employee upon cessation of employment if he or she has rendered continuous service for five years or more, according to Section 4(1) of the Payment of Gratuity Act of 1972. Section 4(2) of the Act provides that for every completed year of service or part thereof in excess of 6 months, the employer shall pay gratuity to an employee at the prescribed rates. The Gratuity Benefits are calculated using the following formula:-(15/26) multiplied by (No of Completed Years on Exit) multiplied by (Terminal Wages/Salary). Under Rule 7(1) of the Payment of Gratuity Rules, 1972, an employee who is eligible for payment of gratuity under the Act, or any person authorized, in writing, to act on his behalf, shall apply, within thirty days from the date the gratuity became payable, in Form 'I' to the employer who is duty bound to disburse the gratuity within 30 days of cessation of employment of employee or claim made by an employee. After 30 days, the employer has to pay you not only the gratuity amount but also the simple interest accrued for the delay in payment of the gratuity. In case of denial of gratuity by the employer, serving a legal notice to the Company/employer reach out to the office of the concerned Labour Commissioner and the Controlling Authority under the Payment of Gratuity Act to file a complaint against the employer over non-payment of gratuity.

question:

2. Is it mandatory for the disciplinary authority to sign the show cause notice themselves?

answer: Dear Client,Background verification(BGV) check is a process many organizations carry out in order to verify the information provided by the candidate during hiring. In case of a negative background verification check an employer can even reject or terminate the employment of the candidate.  Organizations with more than 20 employees must register under the EPF scheme and EPF registration with EPFO is mandatory for salaried employees with an income of up to â¹ 15,000 per month. question: Hello sir, I am a person with benchmark disability. I have locomotor disability of 62% as mentioned in my UDID card. They alloted me a temporary card which is valid for 5 years from the date of issue. Am I eligible for SSC or central government jobs? In the job notification and online form fillup, it's only mentioned as  persons above 40% disability are eligible. I am confused that my certificate which is temporarily valid for 5 years is eligible or not? Sir, please clear my confusion if possible. Thank you Sir.( Cachar, Assam )
answer: Dear Client,The Rights of Persons with Disabilities (RPwD) Act was enacted in the year 2016 and came into force on 19th April 2017. Individuals having 40% or more disability can apply for a disability certificate, provided their disability falls under the categories specified under the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016. Issue of A Unique Disability Identity(UDID) card to a PWD is an initiative by the Government of India with a view of creating a National Database for Persons with Disabilities (PwDs). The UDID card and Disability Certificate have two types of validity- Permanent UDID card and Temporary UDID Card. Permanent UDID: The competent medical authority issues a Permanent UDID Card considering there is no progress or regress in the disability of a PwD. Temporary UDID: The competent medical authority issues a Temporary UDID Card considering there is progress or a regress in the disability of a PwD. A disability certificate remains valid for lifelong in case of a permanent disability. However, for temporary disabilities, the certificate/ID card remains valid for a period of five years. It has to be renewed once in five years subject to the medical examination of the disabled person. So, regardless of the nature and class of PWD and UDID Certificate, a candidate having 40% or more disability can apply for SSC or central government jobs during the period of validity of the UDID Certificate.

I was sent by my ex-employer for a foreign assignment in 2012. As part of the assignment , I signed a agreement that any hypothetical tax paid by the employer shall be paid back when income tax returns pays the amount. For that purpose a escrow account was set up. After completion of the assignment, I resigned from the company in 2016 & later in 2018 from the company's foreign entity and I was given a "No due Certificate". However, the ex-employer is demanding for refund of 6 lakh INR claiming that money had come to my personal account. I am not a indian tax payer since 2016 have no way to verify the actual amount credited and how much of that belongs to the ex-employer. I have asked my ex-eployer to provide me the tax challan. 1. Am i liable to pay any income tax amount credited to my personal account (not escrow) that they have provided no evidence of money being credited. Only evidence provided was filing statement 
2. Can they take a legal action if so what are my rights( Bangalore, Karnataka )
answer: Dear Client,An escrow agreement refers to a contract that outlines the terms and conditions of a transaction for something of value, such as a bond, deed, or asset which is held by a third party until all conditions have been met. An escrow account is opened in the Bank/NBFC following the escrow agreement. Escrow is a legal concept describing a financial agreement whereby an asset or money is held by a third party on behalf of two other parties that are in the process of completing a transaction. The third party holds the funds until both buyer and seller have fulfilled their contractual requirements. If an income from other sources is credited to your personal account, it is taxable once it exceeds the threshold limit of income of the individual assessee, but in the absence of any evidence showing credit of that amount in your personal account, you are not liable to pay tax. The Supreme Court in the issue of CIT v. Shoorji Vallabhdas & Co. held that only real income should be considered for taxation. It was contended that the incidence of taxation arises under the head of âcapital gainsâ on the full value of the consideration that stands accrued as a result of the transfer of capital assets. The law does not provide any form of deduction for money even kept aside in an escrow account and no provision of law permits the deferment of taxation to a later year. So, in the absence of any evidence of credit of the amount, even if the company takes any legal action, you should defend the case, if required hiring the service of a tax professional to navigate the issue in the right way.

question: After serving the organisation for more than 33 years, my payment of gratuity was made after more than one year, and that too in instalments, spread over six months. Employer has refused for payment of interest. My request with Deputy Labour Commissioner (C), Regional Office, New Delhi, is pending since January 2024.( Faridabad, Haryana )
answer: Dear Client,You are on the right track in the fight for your right to gratuity. As per Sub-Section 3 Section 7 of the Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972, the employer shall arrange to pay the amount of gratuity within thirty days from the date it becomes payable to the person to whom the gratuity is payable. As per Sub-Section 3A of Section 7 of the Act, if the amount of gratuity payable under Sub-section (3) is not paid by the employer within the period specified in Sub-section (3), the employer shall pay, from the date on which the gratuity becomes payable to the date on which it is paid, simple interest at such rate, not exceeding the rate notified by the Central Government from time to time for repayment of long-term deposits, as that Government may, by notification specify. Provided that no such interest shall be payable if the delay in the payment is due to the fault of the employee and the employer has obtained permission in writing from the controlling authority for the delayed payment on this ground. Under Sub-Section 4(a) of Sec.7, if there is any dispute as to the amount of gratuity payable to an employee under this Act or as to the admissibility of any claim of, or in relation to, an employee for payment of gratuity, or as to the person entitled to receive the gratuity, the employer shall deposit with the controlling authority such amount as he admits to be payable by him as gratuity. According to Sub-Sec. 4(b) of Sec.7, where there is a dispute with regard to any matter or matters specified in clause (a), the employer or employee or any other person raising the dispute may make an application to the controlling authority for deciding the dispute. Given the provisions of relevant law, when you have filed an application under Sub-Section(1) of Section 7 of the Payment of Gratuity Act read with Rule 9 of the Payment of Gratuity(Central) Rules, 1972 before the Controlling Authority and the Asst. Labour Commissioner concerned seeking payment of interest on delayed payment of gratuity from the employer. Under Sub-Sec.5 of Section 7 of the Act, the Controlling Authority is empowered with the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 to try the claim of the applicant and pass an order/direction on the claim petition.

answer: Dear Client,An employer or an employee can initiate the discharge depending on the situation or consequences. A voluntary discharge means that you resign from a job in compliance with the terms of employment and in that situation, you are entitled to service-linked benefits up to the last date of work(LWD). An involuntary discharge means that an employer dismisses you from the company for a proven act of misconduct and even in that case you are entitled to service-linked benefits up to the last date of work(LWD). on the other hand, if an employee is terminated without cause, they are entitled to receive severance pay. The amount of severance pay is typically one month's salary for every year of service but may be more or less depending on the contract. Any Termination of a workman is covered under the Industrial Disputes Act and it falls under âRetrenchmentâ. In the case of Punjab Land Development Corporation Vs Labour Court, 1990 (II) LLJ, 70 SC, the Supreme Court held that The expression âretrenchmentâ is not to be understood in its narrow, natural and contextual meaning, but is to be understood in its wider, literal meaning to mean termination of service of a workman for any reason whatsoever. Further, in the case of Santosh Gupta Vs State Bank of Patiala AIR 1980 SC 1219, the Supreme Court ruled that the expression retrenchment must include every termination of the services of a workman by an act of the employer.  Under Chapters V-A & V-B of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947, for retrenchment of a workman of an industrial establishment employing below 100 workmen, an employer has to one month's notice or wages in lieu of notice, Compensation of Fifteen days average pay for every completed year of service. 6 months and above to be treated as one year and service of Notice to the appropriate Government(Labour Commissioner). Thus, If an employee is terminated without cause, they are entitled to receive severance pay. The amount of severance pay is typically one month's salary for every year of service but may be more or less depending on the contract. An employee could be entitled to get 'payment in lieu of notice'. This means they stop work straight away but still get paid for their notice period. Termination or dismissal other than a disciplinary action for proven misconduct amounts to illegal termination/retrenchment and is defined as an industrial dispute under Section 2A of the Industrial Dispute Act, 1947 which also violated the mandatory provision of Sec.25F and 25N of the I D Act that prescribed certain conditions to comply with by the employer before termination/retrenchment of a workman/employee from the employment. In that scenario, the terminated employee/workman can raise an industrial dispute before the concerned Labour Commissioner for redressal of the complaint failing which he can approach directly the Industrial Tribunal/Labor Court concerned for adjudication provided he is not holding the position of Manager/Supervisor but a workman as defined u/s.2(s) of the Industrial Dispute Act. Otherwise, in case he is holding the position of Manager/Administrative Officer in the Company, he has to file a civil suit before the Civil Court seeking appropriate relief in the matter.

answer: Dear Client,The relationship between an employee and the employer is governed by the terms of the contract of employment or offer letter. Check your employment contract/leave policy.  If it says it can be encashed then they can't deny it. Leave Encashment Rules for private companies vary according to their policies and local regulations. Subject to the leave encashment policy of the company, an employee who is released on acceptance of his/her resignation shall be allowed encashment of Earned Leave standing to his/her credit as on the date of release post-resignation and service of the notice period.  Acquisitions or mergers of companies also entail the redeployment of human resources or redesigning of roles. Under the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947 the conditions of service of any workman, particularly of any matter specified in the Fourth Schedule, shall not be changed without giving a notice under Section 9A of the Act to the workmen likely to be affected by such change. Schedule Four contains matters like wages, (reduction of wages), contribution paid by the employer to their provident fund or pension fund under any law, compensatory and other allowances, hours of work, leave with wages and holidays, withdrawal of any customary concession or privilege, introduction of new rules of discipline, or alteration of existing rules, etc. The courts in India have ruled that these service conditions cannot be changed without the consent of the affected worker. Section 9A is designed to protect the interests of the âworkmanâ. Where a reference is made at the instance of the employer pursuant to an industrial dispute arising out of a Notice under Section 9A to the detriment of the âworkmanâ, the burden to justify the change lies on the employer. The Supreme Court has observed that a benefit prevailing for long, making it a condition of service, should not be allowed to be interfered with lightly to the prejudice of the workmen in the absence of compelling material. So, If it appears to you that the action of the management is discriminatory and contrary to the provisions of the Industrial Dispute Act, you can escalate your claim before the concerned State Labour Court by filing an application under Sec.33C(2) of the Industrial Dispute Act, 1947, provided you are a workman as defined under Sec.2(s) of the said Act. question: Hi, I had signed a bond for 3years in company, I completed 2 years in that company, now I want to move out of that company, now they are asking me to pay the amount of bond which is 5 lakhs, Can I go legally on this, and how much time does it takes if I go legally?( Hyderabad, Telangana )
answer: Dear Client,A service/employment bond itself does not create any relationship between an employer and an employee unless and until it is followed by the essential steps required to make the Bond valid and enforceable under the law. The validity of Employment bonds can be challenged based on Section 27 of the Indian Contract Act,1872 which prohibits any agreement in restraint of trade and profession. The law states that an agreement (employment bond) will be illegal only if it restrains someone from exercising a lawful profession/ trade/ business. As per the mandate of Section 27 of the Indian Contract Act,1872, any terms and conditions of an agreement that directly or indirectly compels the employee to serve the employer or puts a restriction on them joining the competitor or other employer is not valid. The employee has the right to resign from the employment even if he has agreed to the employment bond to serve the employer for a specific period. In the case where the employer can prove that the employee is joining the competitor to disclose the trade secret then the court may issue an injunction order restricting the employee from joining the competitor. Further, Section 73 of the Act makes provision for un-liquidated damages (not stipulated in a contract), Section 74 deals with liquidated damages (stipulated in a contract) and no compensation is attracted for mere breach of contract u/s.73. 74 of the Act unless such breach resulted in an actual loss or damage to the opposite party employer. So, in the prevailing situation, if you are not holding a position of manager or supervisor in the Company, but a workman as defined under Sec.2(s) of the Industrial Dispute Act, 1947. serving a legal notice to the Company reach out to the office of the concerned Labour Commissioner or the Chief Inspector, Shops and Establishment to file a complaint against the company over alleged unfair labour practice for redressal of your grievance, But, if you are holding the position of Manager or Administrator in the Company, you have to file a civil suit before the Civil Court for desired relief in the matter.

For disabled children below 18 years of age, the card is required to be updated once every five years. No fresh medical examination is necessary in the case of a person with permanent disability. question: My employer is not paying gratuity, i work for 13 years 6 month 23 days( Mumbai suburban, Maharashtra )
answer: Dear Client,An organization/establishment with a workforce of 10 individuals and above is liable to pay gratuity under the Payment of Gratuity Act 1972. Section 4(2) of the Act provides that for every completed year of service or part thereof in excess of 6 months, the employer shall pay gratuity to an employee at the prescribed rates. The Gratuity Benefits are calculated using the following formula:-(15/26) multiplied by (No of Completed Years on Exit) multiplied by (Terminal Wages/Salary). Under Rule 7(1) of the Payment of Gratuity Rules, 1972, an employee who is eligible for payment of gratuity under the Act, or any person authorized, in writing, to act on his behalf, shall apply, within thirty days from the date the gratuity became payable, in Form 'I' to the employer who is duty bound to disburse the gratuity within 30 days of cessation of employment of employee or claim made by an employee. question: My company had a two year contract bond. I left work before that. Now take me legal notice High court( Kolkata, West Bengal )
answer: Dear Client,A service/employment bond itself does not create any relationship between an employer and an employee unless and until it is followed by the essential steps required to make the Bond valid and enforceable under the law. The validity of Employment bonds can be challenged based on Section 27 of the Indian Contract Act,1872 which prohibits any agreement in restraint of trade and profession. The law states that an agreement (employment bond) will be illegal only if it restrains someone from exercising a lawful profession/ trade/ business. As per the mandate of Section 27 of the Indian Contract Act,1872, any terms and conditions of an agreement that directly or indirectly compels the employee to serve the employer or puts a restriction on them joining the competitor or other employer is not valid. The employee has the right to resign from the employment even if he has agreed to the employment bond to serve the employer for a specific period. In the case where the employer can prove that the employee is joining the competitor to disclose the trade secret then the court may issue an injunction order restricting the employee from joining the competitor. Further, Section 73 of the Act makes provision for un-liquidated damages (not stipulated in a contract), Section 74 deals with liquidated damages (stipulated in a contract), and no compensation is attracted for mere breach of contract u/s.73. 74 of the Act unless such breach resulted in an actual loss or damage to the opposite party employer. So, given the proposition of relevant law, on receipt of any legal notice from the employer informing their intention to move High Court, you need to consult with an Advocate experienced in service matters to defend the case suitably before the Court to nullify the claim of the Company.

The purpose of a modal verb is to add meaning to the main verb in a sentence by expressing possibility, ability, permission, or obligation. The most common ones are shall, will, may, should, would and might. âShallâ or "should" is a word of command that imposes a duty or obligation. It requires a specific action to be taken and does not leave room for discretion. âMayâ or "might" in legal terms grants the permission or discretion to act in a certain way, but it is not mandatory. Gives an option for something, that does require it. It is important to distinguish between âmayâ and âshallâ in legal documents, as they convey different meanings. âMayâ indicates permissibility, while âshallâ denotes obligation. The employee has the right to resign from the employment even if he has agreed to the employment bond to serve the employer for a specific period. In the case where the employer can prove that the employee is joining the competitor to disclose the trade secret then the court may issue an injunction order restricting the employee from joining the competitor. Further, Section 73 of the Act makes provision for un-liquidated damages (not stipulated in a contract), Section 74 deals with liquidated damages (stipulated in a contract), and no compensation is attracted for mere breach of contract u/s.73. 74 of the Act unless such breach resulted in an actual loss or damage to the opposite party employer. Regardless of reasons, on cessation of employment, an employee is entitled to an experience certificate, relieving letter and F & F settlement dues from the employer within 30 days of last working days (LWD) and denial of which amounted to unfair labour practices. So, in the prevailing situation, if you are not holding a position of manager or supervisor in the Company, but a workman as defined under Sec.2(s) of the Industrial Dispute Act, 1947. serving a legal notice to the Company reach out to the office of the concerned Labour Commissioner to file a complaint against the company over alleged unfair labour practice for redressal of your grievance, But, if you are holding the position of Manager or Administrator in the Company, you have to file a civil suit against the Company before the Civil Court seeking desired relief in the matter. According to, Section 25C of the Act, the workman who has been laid off is entitled to receive 50 percent of his total basic earnings and a dearness allowance for the duration of the layoff. As per Section 25M, the employer cannot lay off the employee without obtaining permission from the concerned government or the authority as specified by the government. Section 25Q of the Act lays down that when an employer violates the provisions mentioned under Section 25M in such circumstances, he will be held liable for the punishment under this Section 25Q, which is imprisonment, which may extend to one month, a fine, which may be extendable up to one thousand, or both. An employer with more than 50 workers must apply for prior permission of the appropriate government before laying off workers/employees of their establishment under Section 25(M) of the Industrial Dispute Act, 1947. To restrict IT Companies from exploiting their employees by playing double standards, the Division Bench of the Karnataka High Court in the case of Commissioner of Income Tax v. Texas Instruments India Pvt Ltd (2021) 435 ITR unambiguously held that the IT sector employees considered to be "workmen" under Section 2(s) of the Industrial Dispute Act, 1947. Termination without notice amounts to illegal termination and is defined as an industrial dispute under Section 2A of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947 which also violated the mandatory provision of Sec.25F and 25N of the Act that prescribed certain conditions to comply with by the employer before termination/retrenchment of a workman/employee from the employment. In that scenario, the terminated employee/workman can raise an industrial dispute directly before the Industrial Tribunal/Labor Court concerned for adjudication within three years from the date of termination/retrenchment. So, in the prevailing situation, serving a legal notice to the Company, you can raise an Industrial dispute directly before the State Govt. Industrial Tribunal under Sec.2A of the I D Act. and simultaneously file an application u/s.33C(2) of the I D Act before the concerned Labour Court claiming dues from your employer receivable to an employee on illegal termination/retrenchment. . question: I have been made redundant/terminated by my employer stating Less business and the terms& Condition of offer letter paying 1 month pay. I was working with the company last 15 years and the last position was Senior Director.  Company refuse to pay severance pay.  while a month before 6 middle managers have been made redundant and paid severance pay.  can I challenge them to pay severance.  I have completed 58 years 3 days before the termination( Bangalore, Karnataka )
answer: Dear Client,A Director can be removed from the Company either by resignation or by a resolution taken in a special meeting by the shareholders or in some cases, if the articles of association empower the board of Directors to remove a director, subject to the provisions of the Companies Act and the company's articles of association. Regardless of the ground of removal, Directors being removed by shareholders or the board must be given proper notice and an opportunity to present their case before the removal is finalized. In the absence of compliance with these conditions precedent to remove a Director, the action of the board of directors is considered unjust and unfair once the matter is litigated before the NCLT. If any condition is stipulated in the appointment letter of a Director specifying that on failure to meet the business target, the severance package would not be disbursed on cessation of employment for any reason, then the company can deny the payment of severance package to the outgoing Director, otherwise, they cannot. Section 169 of the Companies Act, 2013 mentions the procedure for the removal of the director, allowing for their removal before the expiry of their tenure by passing an ordinary resolution. The section provides that once the notice of the general meeting has been finalized, it shall be accompanied by an explanatory statement to the notice of general meeting, which shall mention the comprehensive grounds for the removal, a copy of the special notice received from a shareholder, and the written presentation given by the director to be removed. The company has to file the necessary returns within thirty days from the date of the ordinary resolution passed in the general meeting. Non-compliance with this may lead to a penalty against the company under Section 117 of the Act. Within 30 days of passing such a resolution, Form MGT 14 and Form DIR 12 are essential to be filed with the Registrar of Companies (ROC). Following the resubmission of Form DIR 12, on the satisfaction of ROC, Form DIR 12 will get approval. The approval time will be between 3 to 6 months from the date of filing of Form DIR 12. Form MGT-14 is basically used to file resolutions. It will be filed by the company within 30 days to the Registrar of Companies (ROC) in compliance with Section 117 of the Act and the rules made thereunder. When the company receives the special notice of intention to move a resolution for the removal of the director, the company shall furnish a copy of the notice and address the director, who will have the right to be heard and make representations against the resolution under Section 169 of the Act. Section 169(8)(a) of the Act mentions that compensation or damages for loss of office may be claimed by a director as per the terms of the contract or terms of his appointment as director, who has been removed as a director consequent to termination of his appointment. However, if the removal complies with the articles of association or terms of service, no compensation may be payable. A director can be removed by the National Company Law Tribunal under Section 242 of the Act. If the members or shareholders file a petition under Section 241 before the tribunal for the prevention of mismanagement and oppression in the company, and if the tribunal deems fit, it may terminate or set aside any contract or agreement made by the director, managing director, or managerial personnel, or order his removal. Rule 30 of the Companies (Management and Administration) Rules, 2014 mentions the penalty for contravention of the rule. In case of any default in compliance with the provisions of this rule, a fine will be imposed on the company and every officer or other person, which may extend to five thousand rupees, and if the contravention continues, it will further extend to five hundred rupees for each day for which the contravention continues. A termination or removal can be challenged by the director under the Companies Act if they believe the removal was unjust, unlawful, or not conducted in compliance with the companyâs articles of association or provisions of the Act. According to the jurisdiction and particulars relating to their removal, directors may take legal action to challenge their removal, including suit or arbitration. They may take action if they believe that the proper procedures were not followed, that the grounds for removal were invalid, or that their removal was on a discriminatory basis or in violation of their rights as directors before the National Company Law Tribunal(NCLT) seeking appropriate relief in the matter.

answer: Dear Client,The whole object of granting a compassionate appointment is to enable the family to tide over the sudden crisis, relieve the deceased's family from financial poverty, and help it get over the emergency. Compassionate appointment is not a vested right or an alternate mode of employment. It is considered and granted strictly following the relevant rules and the scheme. Under the Compassionate Appointments Scheme, employment is offered to any one of the legal heirs of the deceased Public Servant of PSU (i.e.) Wife, Husband, Son, Daughter, Divorcee, Widowed daughter if qualified for the same in terms of rules of compassionate appointment. The eligibility for an appointment under the Scheme for Compassionate Appointment is updated on 02/08/2022 by the Deptt. of Personnel and Training(DOPT), Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievance and Pension, Govt. of India wherein scope and eligibility for employment under the compassionate appointment scheme are explained in detail. The Supreme Courtâs judgment dated May 4, 1994 in the case of Umesh Kumar Nagpal vs. State of Haryana and others [JT 1994(3) S.C. 525] has ruled that offering compassionate appointment as a matter of course irrespective of the financial condition of the family of the deceased or medically retired Government servant is legally impermissible. Compassionate appointment cannot be granted after lapse of a reasonable period and it is not a vested right that can be exercised at any time in the future. The Supreme Court has also held in its judgment dated February 28, 1995 in the case of the Life Insurance Corporation of India vs. Mrs Asha Ramchandra Ambekar and others [JT 1994(2) S.C. 183] that the High Courts and Administrative Tribunals can not give direction for appointment of a person on compassionate grounds but can merely direct consideration of the claim for such an appointment. So, given the above-stated propositions of the Scheme, Court rulings, and the status of your case having a stigma of dismissal, your claim for appointment on compassionate grounds would not be considered or upheld as a matter of right even through litigation. You can go through the complete details and application procedures under the Scheme on Compassionate Appointment on the official website of the DOPT and take steps accordingly if it appears feasible and worthy to you post consultation with an Advocate dealing with CAT/SAT matters.

question:
Under the CCS (Conduct) Rules, 1964, joint representation by  government servants on matters of common interest is prohibited. 

Could you please clarify how has the term 'representation'. been officially defined? Can any communication even if it is not concerned with service matters be called representation or only those communications which pertain only to service related matters and any claim, demand, complain, or grievance in respect thereof are representations.( Varanasi, Uttar Pradesh )
answer: Dear Client,As per DOPT OM No. 11013/11/97-Estt.(A), dated 06.11.1997 The representations from Government servants on service matters are broadly classified as follows - (1) Representations/complaints regarding non-payment of salary/allowances or other dues; (2) Representations on other service matters; (3) Representations against the orders of the immediate superior authority; and (4) Appeals and petitions under statutory rules and orders (e.g. Classification, Control and Appeal Rules and the petition Instructions). Any representation other than these classified representations if made by a public servant without proper channels i.e, routed through HOD is considered a violation of Rule 20 of the CCS (Conduct) Rules, 1964. Hope the matter stands clarified.

question: I have signed bond for 3 years but they haven't spend single rupee for my training is this bond is legal? If not what should I do to break the bond ? (They are asking me to pay three month gross salary as penalty)( Bangalore, Karnataka )
answer: Dear Client,A service/employment bond itself does not create any relationship between an employer and an employee unless and until it is followed by the essential steps required to make the Bond valid and enforceable under the law. The validity of Employment bonds can be challenged based on Section 27 of the Indian Contract Act,1872 which prohibits any agreement in restraint of trade and profession. The law states that an agreement (employment bond) will be illegal only if it restrains someone from exercising a lawful profession/ trade/ business. As per the mandate of Section 27 of the Indian Contract Act,1872, any terms and conditions of an agreement that directly or indirectly compels the employee to serve the employer or puts a restriction on them joining the competitor or other employer is not valid. The employee has the right to resign from the employment even if he has agreed to the employment bond to serve the employer for a specific period. In the case where the employer can prove that the employee is joining the competitor to disclose the trade secret then the court may issue an injunction order restricting the employee from joining the competitor. Further, Section 73 of the Act makes provision for un-liquidated damages (not stipulated in a contract), Section 74 deals with liquidated damages (stipulated in a contract), and no compensation is attracted for mere breach of contract u/s.73. 74 of the Act unless such breach resulted in an actual loss or damage to the opposite party employer. So, in the prevailing situation, if the Company takes any legal action against you or terminates your service without notice or without compliance with the provision of Sec.25F or 25N of the Industrial Dispute Act, 1947 and you are not holding the position of Manager/Supervisor but a workman as defined u/s.2(s) of the Industrial Dispute Act then after serving a legal notice to the Company, reach out to the office of the Labour Commissioner concerned for filing a complaint against the employer over alleged unfair labour practice to resolve the grievance, Additionally you need to file an application under Section 33C(2) o the I D Act before the State Labour Court claiming F & F settlement dues with interest from the Company.  Reach out to an Advocate for guidance and steps.

Otherwise, if you were holding the position of Manager or Administrative Officer in the company then you have to file a civil suit against the company for recovery of your dues.

question: My previous employer incorrectly filled out my PF details, leading to my new employer revoking my appointment due to a failed background verification. Despite my repeated reminders, they failed to rectify the error. Now that they have finally submitted the corrected information, I intend to pursue legal action against both my former employer and the EPFO office. It's worth noting that I reside in a different city from where the company is located.( Dehradun, Uttarakhand )
answer: Dear Client,If your previous employer incorrectly filled out your Provident Fund (PF) details, resulting in your new employer revoking your appointment due to a failed background verification, and despite your repeated reminders, they failed to rectify the error in a timely manner, you have grounds to pursue legal action. Here's how you can proceed:Send a Legal Notice: Start by sending a legal notice to your previous employer and the EPFO office, outlining the issue and the damages you have suffered as a result of their negligence. This can be done through a lawyer.File a Complaint with the EPFO: You can file a formal complaint with the EPFO office regarding the incorrect details and the delay in correction. This can be done online through the EPFO grievance portal.Consumer Court: Since you have suffered a loss due to the deficiency in service provided by your previous employer and the EPFO office, you can file a case in the Consumer Court. This is applicable under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, which protects consumers against deficient services.Civil Suit for Damages: You can also file a civil suit for damages against your previous employer for the loss of employment opportunity. This would involve proving the negligence and the impact it had on your career and financial status.Jurisdiction: Since you reside in a different city from where the company is located, you can file the case in the jurisdiction where the cause of action occurred or where you currently reside. The Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, allows for such provisions.Documentation: Collect all relevant documents, including email correspondence, the PF details provided by your previous employer, the background verification report, the job offer revocation letter from your new employer, and any communication with the EPFO office.Legal Counsel: Consult with a lawyer who specializes in employment law and consumer rights. They can guide you through the process and help you draft the necessary legal documents.By following these steps, you can seek redressal for the inconvenience and financial loss you have suffered due to the negligence of your previous employer and the EPFO office.

question: I was in judicial custody on IPC 304 B. The organization has sent me abandonment letter while I have informed all the things to reporting manager and organization.Now I am on bail and want reinstate my job but the organization is saying there is no vacancy and they have hired someone on my role.( Gurgaon, Haryana )
answer: Dear Client,Abandonment from employment is considered an unauthorized absence from a job and misconduct on the part of the abandoned employee. Accordingly, an employer can take disciplinary action against the abandoned employee including striking off his name from the permanent role of the Company. Moreover, conviction by a court of law for a criminal offense is a moral turpitude and misconduct that attracts disciplinary action, including dismissal of an employee on proven misconduct established in the employer's domestic inquiry proceedings. Even, if you are released on bail, your claim for reinstatement will not be entertained/considered until and unless you are acquitted of the criminal charges by the Court. After acquittal from the criminal charges, you may raise an industrial dispute before the Industrial Tribunal/Labour Court claiming your reinstatement in service with back wages. But the chance of winning the dispute is not feasible at the moment if the pleadings of employers override the merit in your claim.

question: I got a central government job in NPCIL. They have asked me to mention in SSQ  if there are any pending cases on my parents. There is a pending criminal case U/s 420 and 34 on my father. All columns for these forms are required to be filled correctly and completely and in case the space provided in any of the columns is not sufficient for furnishing the information sought, the candidate can utilize an extra sheet. No column should be left blank and N/A may be mentioned in case no information is to be provided. Suppression of facts or providing false/ incorrect information in the Attestation Form(AF) & SSQ could result in cancellation of candidature at any stage of the recruitment process and even after the contractual appointment if noticed subsequently. Final selection is subject to the performance of the candidate in the interview and successful completion of C & A (Character & Antecedents) verification and medical examination if required. The duly filled-in AF and SSQ forms are required to be deposited by the candidate on the day of the interview. In view of the above, until and unless a criminal prosecution is dismissed or disposed of by the Cout acquitting the accused from the criminal charge, you cannot mention in the SSQ Form that your father was not accused of any criminal charge or that no criminal case is pending against your father on the date of application or subsequent selection process for a central government job. The suppression of factual information may liable you to face cancellation of candidature/appointment and other legal consequences later on if it is unearthed in the course of police verification of your candidature based on SSQ and the records maintained by the National Crime Record Bureau (NCRB),

question: Sir I want to know that where should I consult to resolve the overlapping date in my PF Account . My employer is not ready to solve it from my end .( Meerut, Uttar Pradesh )

It is a combined form that the employee and employer sign and submit to the regional PF commissioner to rectify and update the information entered in the employeesâ PF accounts. Only an employer can rectify the error in the employment record of the EPFO. So if an employee finds an error in the database of EPF Account, he/she should contact present or previous employers and get it corrected.  In the given situation, to resolve the issue of dual employment or overlapping in the P F records of both employers, you need to approach the office of the Regional P F Commissioner who is the competent authority to resolve any anomaly/discrepancy arising out of the date of appointment and date of exit in EPF records. So, if no relief yields from the office of the PF Commissioner, you may approach the Central Government Industrial Tribunal for appropriate relief.
